rohiṇyā sārdhamavasadratotsavakalādibhiḥ || 30 ||
2.d:
अथ चन्द्रः समस्तासु तासु कन्यासु रागतः ।
रोहिण्या सार्धमवसद्रतोत्सवकलादिभिः ॥ 30 ॥
2.m: Then the moon, out of passion, among all those maidens, / dwelt only with Rohiṇī, indulging in sexual delights, the [erotic] arts, and the like.

2.s:
rohiṇīmeva bhajate rohiṇyā saha modate |
vinendū rohiṇī śāntiṃ na kāñcillabhate purā || 31 ||
2.d:
रोहिणीमेव भजते रोहिण्या सह मोदते ।
विनेन्दू रोहिणी शान्तिं न काञ्चिल्लभते पुरा ॥ 31 ॥
2.m: He attended to Rohiṇī alone, he rejoiced with Rohiṇī; / of old, Rohiṇī found no peace whatsoever without the moon.

2.s:
rohiṇītatparaṃ candraṃ vīkṣya tāḥ sarvakanyakāḥ |
upacārairbahuvidhairbhejuścandramasaṃ prati || 32 ||
2.d:
रोहिणीतत्परं चन्द्रं वीक्ष्य ताः सर्वकन्यकाः ।
उपचारैर्बहुविधैर्भेजुश्चन्द्रमसं प्रति ॥ 32 ॥
2.m: Seeing the moon devoted solely to Rohiṇī, all those maidens / worshipped the moon with various kinds of attentive service.

2.s:
niṣevyamāṇo'nudinaṃ yadā naivākarodvidhuḥ |
tāsu bhāvaṃ tadā sarvā amarṣavaśamāgatāḥ || 33 ||
2.d:
निषेव्यमाणोऽनुदिनं यदा नैवाकरोद्विधुः ।
तासु भावं तदा सर्वा अमर्षवशमागताः ॥ 33 ॥
2.m: When, though attended day after day, the moon did not / bestow his affection on them, they all fell under the sway of indignation.

2.s:
athottarāphālgunīti nāmnā yā bharaṇī tathā |
kṛttikārdrā maghā caiva viśākhottarabhādrapat || 34 ||
2.d:
अथोत्तराफाल्गुनीति नाम्ना या भरणी तथा ।
कृत्तिकार्द्रा मघा चैव विशाखोत्तरभाद्रपत् ॥ 34 ॥
2.m: Then she who is named Uttarāphālgunī, and Bharaṇī, / Kṛttikā, Ārdrā, Maghā, Viśākhā, Uttarabhādrapadā,

2.s:
tathā jyeṣṭhottarāṣāḍhe navaitāḥ kupitāḥ bhṛśam |
himāṃśumupasaṃgamya parivavruḥ samantataḥ || 35 ||
2.d:
तथा ज्येष्ठोत्तराषाढे नवैताः कुपिताः भृशम् ।
हिमांशुमुपसंगम्य परिवव्रुः समन्ततः ॥ 35 ॥
2.m: and likewise Jyeṣṭhā and Uttarāṣāḍhā—these nine, greatly enraged, / approached the cold-rayed [moon] and surrounded him on all sides.

2.s:
parivārya niśānāthaṃ dadṛśū rohiṇīṃ tataḥ |
vāmāṃkasthā tasya tena ramamāṇāṃ svamaṇḍale || 36 ||
2.d:
परिवार्य निशानाथं ददृशू रोहिणीं ततः ।
वामांकस्था तस्य तेन रममाणां स्वमण्डले ॥ 36 ॥
2.m: Having surrounded the lord of night, they then saw Rohiṇī / sitting on his left lap, delighting with him in his orb.

2.s:
tāṃ vīkṣya tādṛśīṃ sarvā rohiṇīṃ varavarṇinīm |
jajvaluścātikopena haviṣeva hutāśanaḥ || 37 ||
2.d:
तां वीक्ष्य तादृशीं सर्वा रोहिणीं वरवर्णिनीम् ।
जज्वलुश्चातिकोपेन हविषेव हुताशनः ॥ 37 ॥
2.m: Beholding that beautiful Rohiṇī in such a state, they all / blazed with intense fury, like fire fed with clarified butter.

2.s:
tato maghātripūrvāśca bharaṇī kṛttikā tathā |
candrāṃkasthāṃ mahābhāgāṃ rohiṇī jagṛhuhaṃṭhāt || 38 ||
2.d:
ततो मघात्रिपूर्वाश्च भरणी कृत्तिका तथा ।
चन्द्रांकस्थां महाभागां रोहिणी जगृहुहंठात् ॥ 38 ॥
2.m: Then Maghā, the three Pūrvās, Bharaṇī, and Kṛttikā / forcibly seized the illustrious Rohiṇī as she sat on the moon’s lap.

2.s:
ūcuścātīva kupitāḥ puruṣaṃ rohiṇī prati |
jīvannyā tvayi duṣprājñe nāsmānindustu bhāvabhāk || 39 ||
2.d:
ऊचुश्चातीव कुपिताः पुरुषं रोहिणी प्रति ।
जीवन्न्या त्वयि दुष्प्राज्ञे नास्मानिन्दुस्तु भावभाक् ॥ 39 ॥
2.m: And exceedingly wrathful, they said to Rohiṇī before her husband: / “While you are alive, O foolish woman, the moon does not turn his affection toward us!

2.s:
samupaiṣyati kasmiścitsamaye suratotsukaḥ |
vahvīnāṃ kṣemavṛddhyarthaṃ tāṃ haniṣyāmaṃ durmatim || 40 ||
2.d:
समुपैष्यति कस्मिश्चित्समये सुरतोत्सुकः ।
वह्वीनां क्षेमवृद्ध्यर्थं तां हनिष्यामं दुर्मतिम् ॥ 40 ॥
2.m: Eager for sexual pleasure, he will approach [us] at some time; / for the sake of the welfare and prosperity of many, we shall kill that wicked-minded woman!

2.s:
na tvāṃ hatvā bhavet pāpamasmākamapi kiṃcana |
prajanaghnī bahustrīṇāmanṛtau pāpakāriṇīm || 41 ||
2.d:
न त्वां हत्वा भवेत् पापमस्माकमपि किंचन ।
प्रजनघ्नी बहुस्त्रीणामनृतौ पापकारिणीम् ॥ 41 ॥
2.m: No sin whatsoever will befall us from slaying you, / an evil-doer who destroys the procreation of many women out of season.

2.s:
yasminnarthe purā brahmā vyājahāra suta prati |
tītiśāstropadeśāya tanna saṃśrutamasti vai || 42 ||
2.d:
यस्मिन्नर्थे पुरा ब्रह्मा व्याजहार सुत प्रति ।
तीतिशास्त्रोपदेशाय तन्न संश्रुतमस्ति वै ॥ 42 ॥
2.m: On this matter, what Brahmā of old declared to his son / for the instruction of the treatises on moral conduct, has that not indeed been heard by you?

2.s:
ekasya yatra nidhane pravṛtte duṣṭakāriṇaḥ |
bahunā bhavati kṣema tasya puṇyaprado vadhaḥ || 43 ||
2.d:
एकस्य यत्र निधने प्रवृत्ते दुष्टकारिणः ।
बहुना भवति क्षेम तस्य पुण्यप्रदो वधः ॥ 43 ॥
2.m: ‘When the destruction of a single wrongdoer is undertaken, / if welfare accrues to many, the slaying of that person brings merit.

2.s:
rukmasteyī surāpaśca brahmahā gurutalpagaḥ |
ātmānaṃ ghātayedyastu tasya puṇyaprado vadhaḥ || 44 ||
2.d:
रुक्मस्तेयी सुरापश्च ब्रह्महा गुरुतल्पगः ।
आत्मानं घातयेद्यस्तु तस्य पुण्यप्रदो वधः ॥ 44 ॥
2.m: A thief of gold, a drinker of liquor, a slayer of a brāhmaṇa, and one who violates the teacher’s bed— / when someone kills such a person, their slaying brings merit.’”

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
tāsāṃ tādṛgabhiprāyaṃ buddhā dṛṣṭvā ca karma ca |
bhītāṃ ca rohiṇīṃ dṛṣṭvā priyāmatimanoramām || 45 ||
2.d:
तासां तादृगभिप्रायं बुद्धा दृष्ट्वा च कर्म च ।
भीतां च रोहिणीं दृष्ट्वा प्रियामतिमनोरमाम् ॥ 45 ॥
2.m: Perceiving such an intention of theirs and seeing their action, / and seeing his frightened, exceedingly charming beloved Rohiṇī,

2.s:
ātmānaṃ cāparādhaṃ ca tadasambhogajaṃ muhuḥ |
vicintya rohiṇīṃ bhītāṃ tāsāṃ hastādamocayat || 46 ||
2.d:
आत्मानं चापराधं च तदसम्भोगजं मुहुः ।
विचिन्त्य रोहिणीं भीतां तासां हस्तादमोचयत् ॥ 46 ॥
2.m: and reflecting repeatedly upon himself and his own fault born of failing to enjoy them, / he freed the frightened Rohiṇī from their hands.

2.s:
mocayitvā ca bāhubhyāṃ sampariṣvajya rohiṇīm |
vārayāmāsa tāḥ sarvāḥ kṛttikādyāḥ sa bhāminīḥ || 47 ||
2.d:
मोचयित्वा च बाहुभ्यां सम्परिष्वज्य रोहिणीम् ।
वारयामास ताः सर्वाः कृत्तिकाद्याः स भामिनीः ॥ 47 ॥
2.m: And having freed Rohiṇī and embraced her closely with both arms, / he restrained all those angry women beginning with Kṛttikā.

2.s:
tadenduṃ vārayantyastāḥ kṛttikādyā maghāntakāḥ |
sāmyamūcurmanasvinyastāṃ vīkṣyantyo'tha rohiṇīm || 48 ||
2.d:
तदेन्दुं वारयन्त्यस्ताः कृत्तिकाद्या मघान्तकाः ।
साम्यमूचुर्मनस्विन्यस्तां वीक्ष्यन्त्योऽथ रोहिणीम् ॥ 48 ॥
2.m: Then those spirited women beginning with Kṛttikā and ending with Maghā, holding back the moon, / spoke with composure, looking at Rohiṇī:

2.s:
na te trapā vā bhītirvā pāpato'smānnirasyataḥ |
saṃjāyate niśānātha prākṛtasyeva vartataḥ || 49 ||
2.d:
न ते त्रपा वा भीतिर्वा पापतोऽस्मान्निरस्यतः ।
संजायते निशानाथ प्राकृतस्येव वर्ततः ॥ 49 ॥
2.m: “Have you no shame or fear of sin as you cast us aside, / O lord of night, behaving just like a common man?

2.s:
kathamasmānnirākṛtya cāritravratadhāriṇīḥ |
sadā bhaktimatīrekāṃ mūḍhavattvaṃ niṣevase || 50 ||
2.d:
कथमस्मान्निराकृत्य चारित्रव्रतधारिणीः ।
सदा भक्तिमतीरेकां मूढवत्त्वं निषेवसे ॥ 50 ॥
2.m: How can you, having spurned us who observe the vows of good conduct / and are ever devoted, attend like a fool to one alone?

2.s:
ki te nāvagato dharmo vedamūlaḥ śrutaḥ purā |
yaddharmahīna kuruṣa karma sadbhivigahitam || 51 ||
2.d:
कि ते नावगतो धर्मो वेदमूलः श्रुतः पुरा ।
यद्धर्महीन कुरुष कर्म सद्भिविगहितम् ॥ 51 ॥
2.m: Did you not understand righteousness, rooted in the Veda, which was heard in the past, / that, devoid of righteousness, you perform an act despised by the virtuous?

2.s:
dharmaśāstrārthagaṃ karma carantīnā yathocitam |
kathamudvāhitānā tvaṃ mukhamātra na vīkṣase || 52 ||
2.d:
धर्मशास्त्रार्थगं कर्म चरन्तीना यथोचितम् ।
कथमुद्वाहिताना त्वं मुखमात्र न वीक्षसे ॥ 52 ॥
2.m: How can you not even look at the face of us who have been married [to you], / as we act as is proper, engaging in deeds following the meaning of the treatises on dharma?

2.s:
gadato yacchruta pūrva nāradāya piturmukhāt |
dakṣasya dharmaśāstrārtha tacchṛṇuṣva niśāpate || 53 ||
2.d:
गदतो यच्छ्रुत पूर्व नारदाय पितुर्मुखात् ।
दक्षस्य धर्मशास्त्रार्थ तच्छृणुष्व निशापते ॥ 53 ॥
2.m: Listen, O lord of night, to the meaning of the treatises on dharma spoken of old / by Dakṣa from his father’s mouth, as heard being proclaimed to Nārada:

2.s:
bahudāraḥ pumān yastu rāgādekāṃ bhajet striyam |
sa pāpabhākstrījitaśca tasyāśaucaṃ sanātanam ||54 ||
2.d:
बहुदारः पुमान् यस्तु रागादेकां भजेत् स्त्रियम् ।
स पापभाक्स्त्रीजितश्च तस्याशौचं सनातनम् ॥54 ॥
2.m: ‘A man who has many wives, but out of passion consorts with only one woman, / is a partaker of sin, subjugated by a woman, and his impurity is perpetual.

2.s:
yadduḥkhaṃ jāyate strīṇāṃ svāmyasambhogajaṃ vidho |
na tasya sadṛśaṃ dukhaṃ kiñcidanyatra vidyate || 55 ||
2.d:
यद्दुःखं जायते स्त्रीणां स्वाम्यसम्भोगजं विधो ।
न तस्य सदृशं दुखं किञ्चिदन्यत्र विद्यते ॥ 55 ॥
2.m: The sorrow that arises for women from not being enjoyed by their husband, O moon, / there is no other sorrow anywhere that resembles it.

2.s:
satīmṛtumaīṃ jāyāṃ yo neyātpuruṣādhamaḥ |
ṛtughasreṣu śuddheṣu bhrūṇahā sa ca jāyate || 56 ||
2.d:
सतीमृतुमईं जायां यो नेयात्पुरुषाधमः ।
ऋतुघस्रेषु शुद्धेषु भ्रूणहा स च जायते ॥ 56 ॥
2.m: That lowest of men who does not approach his faithful wife when she has had her season / during the pure days of her season, becomes a slayer of an embryo.

2.s:
bhāryā syādayāvadātreyī tāvatkālaṃ vibodhanam |
tasyāstu saṃgame kiṃcidvihitañcāpi nācaret || 57 ||
2.d:
भार्या स्यादयावदात्रेयी तावत्कालं विबोधनम् ।
तस्यास्तु संगमे किंचिद्विहितञ्चापि नाचरेत् ॥ 57 ॥
2.m: As long as a wife has her menses, during that time there is an injunction: / one should not engage in anything prescribed for union with her.

2.s:
bahubhāryasya bhāryāṇāmṛtumaithunanāśanam |
na kiṃcidvidyate karma śāstreṇāpi yadīritam || 58 ||
2.d:
बहुभार्यस्य भार्याणामृतुमैथुननाशनम् ।
न किंचिद्विद्यते कर्म शास्त्रेणापि यदीरितम् ॥ 58 ॥
2.m: For a man of many wives, the destruction of his wives’ fertile season and intercourse— / there is no deed [worse] which has been spoken of even by sacred tradition.

2.s:
toṣayet satataṃ bhāryāvidhivatpāṇipīḍitāḥ |
tāsāṃ tuṣṭyā tu kalyāṇamakalyāṇamato'nyathā || 59 ||
2.d:
तोषयेत् सततं भार्याविधिवत्पाणिपीडिताः ।
तासां तुष्ट्या तु कल्याणमकल्याणमतोऽन्यथा ॥ 59 ॥
2.m: He should always satisfy his wives whose hands he has taken according to rule; / through their contentment there is prosperity, but otherwise, misfortune.

2.s:
santuṣṭo bhāryayā bhartā bhatrā bhāryā tathaiva ca |
yasminnetatkule nityaṃ kalyāṇaṃ tatra vai dhruvam || 60 ||
2.d:
सन्तुष्टो भार्यया भर्ता भत्रा भार्या तथैव च ।
यस्मिन्नेतत्कुले नित्यं कल्याणं तत्र वै ध्रुवम् ॥ 60 ॥
2.m: The husband is pleased with the wife, and the wife likewise with the husband; / in whichever family this is constant, auspicious fortune is indeed certain there.

2.s:
yayā virudhyate svāmī saubhāgyamadadṛptayā |
sapatnīsaṃgamaṃ kartuṃ sā syādveśyā bhavāntare || 61 ||
2.d:
यया विरुध्यते स्वामी सौभाग्यमददृप्तया ।
सपत्नीसंगमं कर्तुं सा स्याद्वेश्या भवान्तरे ॥ 61 ॥
2.m: She who, arrogant with the pride of good fortune, opposes her husband / in having union with her co-wives, will become a courtesan in another birth.

2.s:
ihāpi loke vācyatvamadharmañcāpi vindati |
na pituśca kula svāmikula tasyā pramodate || 62 ||
2.d:
इहापि लोके वाच्यत्वमधर्मञ्चापि विन्दति ।
न पितुश्च कुल स्वामिकुल तस्या प्रमोदते ॥ 62 ॥
2.m: Even in this world she incurs reproach and unrighteousness; / neither her father’s family nor her husband’s family rejoices in her.

2.s:
virudhyamāne patyo yatsapatnyā vā pravartate |
atīva duḥkha bhavati tadakalyāṇakṛttayo || 63 ||
2.d:
विरुध्यमाने पत्यो यत्सपत्न्या वा प्रवर्तते ।
अतीव दुःख भवति तदकल्याणकृत्तयो ॥ 63 ॥
2.m: When opposition to the husband arises on the part of a co-wife, / there is great sorrow, and it brings misfortune to the two of them.’”

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
ityeva bhāṣabhāṇās tāsu cātīva niṣṭhuram |
cukopa candramā dṛṣṭvā malinaṃ rohiṇīmukham || 64 ||
2.d:
इत्येव भाषभाणास् तासु चातीव निष्ठुरम् ।
चुकोप चन्द्रमा दृष्ट्वा मलिनं रोहिणीमुखम् ॥ 64 ॥
2.m: While they were speaking thus, exceedingly harshly to them, / the Moon, seeing Rohiṇī’s face darkened, became enraged.

2.s:
rohiṇī ca tadā tāsāmavalokyogratāṃ muhuḥ |
na kiṃcit sāpi provāca bhayaśokatrapākulā || 65 ||
2.d:
रोहिणी च तदा तासामवलोक्योग्रतां मुहुः ।
न किंचित् सापि प्रोवाच भयशोकत्रपाकुला ॥ 65 ॥
2.m: Rohiṇī too, repeatedly observing their fury at that time, / said nothing at all, overwhelmed by fear, grief, and shame.

2.s:
athāpi kupitaścandrastāḥ śaśāpa tadā striyaḥ |
yasmānmama puraścogrāstīkṣṇā vācaḥ samīritāḥ || 66 ||
2.d:
अथापि कुपितश्चन्द्रस्ताः शशाप तदा स्त्रियः ।
यस्मान्मम पुरश्चोग्रास्तीक्ष्णा वाचः समीरिताः ॥ 66 ॥
2.m: Then the enraged Moon cursed those women: / “Because fierce and sharp words were spoken before me

2.s:
bhavatībhiśca tisṛbhiloke'smin kṛttikādibhiḥ |
ūgrāstīkṣṇā iti khyātiḥ prāptavyā tridaśeṣvapi || 67 ||
2.d:
भवतीभिश्च तिसृभिलोकेऽस्मिन् कृत्तिकादिभिः ।
ऊग्रास्तीक्ष्णा इति ख्यातिः प्राप्तव्या त्रिदशेष्वपि ॥ 67 ॥
2.m: by you three and the others beginning with Kṛttikā, in this world / you shall attain the reputation of being ‘fierce’ and ‘sharp’ even among the gods.

2.s:
tasmādevaṃvidhānena navaitāḥ kṛttikādayaḥ |
yātrāyāṃ nopayuktā hi bhaviṣyadhvaṃ dine dine || 68 ||
2.d:
तस्मादेवंविधानेन नवैताः कृत्तिकादयः ।
यात्रायां नोपयुक्ता हि भविष्यध्वं दिने दिने ॥ 68 ॥
2.m: Therefore, through such a decree, these nine [asterisms] beginning with Kṛttikā / shall indeed become unfit for journeys day after day.

2.s:
yuṣmān paśyanti devādyā manuṣyādyā ca ye kṣitau |
yātrāyāṃ tena doṣeṇa teṣāṃ yātrā na ceṣṭadā || 69 ||
2.d:
युष्मान् पश्यन्ति देवाद्या मनुष्याद्या च ये क्षितौ ।
यात्रायां तेन दोषेण तेषां यात्रा न चेष्टदा ॥ 69 ॥
2.m: The gods and mortals on earth who gaze upon you / on a journey—by that flaw their journey shall not grant their desire.”

2.s:
atha sarvāstadā śāpaṃ tasya śrutvātidāruṇam |
candrasya hṛdayaṃ jñātvā śāpāccātīva niṣṭhuram || 70 ||
2.d:
अथ सर्वास्तदा शापं तस्य श्रुत्वातिदारुणम् ।
चन्द्रस्य हृदयं ज्ञात्वा शापाच्चातीव निष्ठुरम् ॥ 70 ॥
2.m: Then, having heard his exceedingly dreadful curse, / and knowing the Moon’s heart to be even harsher than the curse,

2.s:
jagmuḥ sarvāstadā dakṣabhavanaṃ pratyamarṣitāḥ |
ūcuśca dakṣaṃ pitaramaśvinyādyāḥ sagadgadam || 71 ||
2.d:
जग्मुः सर्वास्तदा दक्षभवनं प्रत्यमर्षिताः ।
ऊचुश्च दक्षं पितरमश्विन्याद्याः सगद्गदम् ॥ 71 ॥
2.m: all of them went angrily to Dakṣa’s abode; / and Aśvinī and the others spoke stammeringly to their father Dakṣa:

2.s:
somo vasati nāsmāsu rohiṇīṃ bhajate sadā |
sevamānā na bhajate so'smān paravadhūriva || 72 ||
2.d:
सोमो वसति नास्मासु रोहिणीं भजते सदा ।
सेवमाना न भजते सोऽस्मान् परवधूरिव ॥ 72 ॥
2.m: “Soma does not dwell with us; he always attends upon Rohiṇī. / Though we serve him, he does not attend upon us, as though we were the wives of others.

2.s:
nāvasthāne nāvasāne bhojane śravaṇe tathā |
vinendū rohiṇīṃ śāntiṃ labhate nahi kāṃcana || 73 ||
2.d:
नावस्थाने नावसाने भोजने श्रवणे तथा ।
विनेन्दू रोहिणीं शान्तिं लभते नहि कांचन ॥ 73 ॥
2.m: Neither in resting nor in waking, neither in eating nor in listening— / without Rohiṇī the Moon finds no peace whatsoever.

2.s:
rohiṇyā vasatastasya samīpaṃ vīkṣya te sutāḥ |
yāntīḥ so'nyatra nayanamādhāya nahi vīkṣate || 74 ||
2.d:
रोहिण्या वसतस्तस्य समीपं वीक्ष्य ते सुताः ।
यान्तीः सोऽन्यत्र नयनमाधाय नहि वीक्षते ॥ 74 ॥
2.m: When your daughters, who reside there, are seen approaching near him, / he turns his eyes elsewhere while Rohiṇī stays [with him], and does not look [at them].

2.s:
māstvanyaḥ svāmisadbhāvo mukhamātraṃ na vīkṣate |
asmin vastuni yatkāryaṃ tadasmābhirnigadyatām || 75 ||
2.d:
मास्त्वन्यः स्वामिसद्भावो मुखमात्रं न वीक्षते ।
अस्मिन् वस्तुनि यत्कार्यं तदस्माभिर्निगद्यताम् ॥ 75 ॥
2.m: Let alone any other husbandly affection, he does not look even at our faces. / In this matter, let what must be done be declared by you to us.

2.s:
asmābhiretsamaye'nuruddhaśca candramāḥ |
sa tatkṛte tataścāsmacchāpaṃ tīvra tadākarot || 76 ||
2.d:
अस्माभिरेत्समयेऽनुरुद्धश्च चन्द्रमाः ।
स तत्कृते ततश्चास्मच्छापं तीव्र तदाकरोत् ॥ 76 ॥
2.m: At this time the Moon was rebuked by us, / and on that account he then laid a terrible curse upon us:

2.s:
dāruṇāścātitīkṣṇāśca loke vācyatvamāpya ca |
ayātrikā bhaviṣyadhvaṃ yūyamityuktavān vidhuḥ || 77 ||
2.d:
दारुणाश्चातितीक्ष्णाश्च लोके वाच्यत्वमाप्य च ।
अयात्रिका भविष्यध्वं यूयमित्युक्तवान् विधुः ॥ 77 ॥
2.m: ‘Becoming known in the world as dreadful and exceedingly sharp, / you shall become inauspicious for journeys’—so the Moon declared.”

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
śrutvā vākyaṃ sa putrīṇāṃ tābhiḥ sārdhaṃ prajāpatiḥ |
jagāma yatra somo'bhūdrohiṇyā sahitastadā || 78 ||
2.d:
श्रुत्वा वाक्यं स पुत्रीणां ताभिः सार्धं प्रजापतिः ।
जगाम यत्र सोमोऽभूद्रोहिण्या सहितस्तदा ॥ 78 ॥
2.m: Hearing the words of his daughters, Prajāpati [Dakṣa], along with them, / went to where Soma was with Rohiṇī at that time.

2.s:
dūrādeva vidhurdṛṣṭvā dakṣamāyāntamāsanāt |
uttasthāvantike prāpya vavande ca mahāmunim || 79 ||
2.d:
दूरादेव विधुर्दृष्ट्वा दक्षमायान्तमासनात् ।
उत्तस्थावन्तिके प्राप्य ववन्दे च महामुनिम् ॥ 79 ॥
2.m: Seeing Dakṣa arriving from afar, the Moon rose from his seat, / approached him, and bowed to the great sage.

2.s:
atha dakṣastadovāca kṛtāsanaparigrahaḥ |
sāmapūrvaṃ candramasaṃ kṛta-saṃvandanaṃ tathā || 80 ||
2.d:
अथ दक्षस्तदोवाच कृतासनपरिग्रहः ।
सामपूर्वं चन्द्रमसं कृत-संवन्दनं तथा ॥ 80 ॥
2.m: Then Dakṣa, having accepted a seat, / spoke with conciliation to the Moon, who had thus paid homage to him.

2.s: dakṣa uvāca
2.d: दक्ष उवाच

2.s:
samaṃ vartasva bhāryāsu vaiṣamyaṃ tvaṃ parityaja |
vaiṣamye bahavo doṣā brahmaṇā parikīrtitāḥ || 81 ||
2.d:
समं वर्तस्व भार्यासु वैषम्यं त्वं परित्यज ।
वैषम्ये बहवो दोषा ब्रह्मणा परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 81 ॥
2.m: “Behave equally toward your wives; abandon partiality. / Many faults in partiality have been proclaimed by Brahmā.

2.s:
ratiputraphalā dārāstāsu kāmānubandhanāt |
kāmānubandhaḥ saṃsargāt saṃsargaḥ saṃgamādbhavet || 82 ||
2.d:
रतिपुत्रफला दारास्तासु कामानुबन्धनात् ।
कामानुबन्धः संसर्गात् संसर्गः संगमाद्भवेत् ॥ 82 ॥
2.m: Wives yield the fruit of sexual pleasure and sons through the binding of desire in them. / The binding of desire comes from company, and company comes from union.

2.s:
saṃgamaścāpyabhidhyānādvīkṣaṇādabhijāyate |
tasmād bhāryāsvabhidhyānaṃ kuru tvaṃ vīkṣaṇādikam || 83 ||
2.d:
संगमश्चाप्यभिध्यानाद्वीक्षणादभिजायते ।
तस्माद् भार्यास्वभिध्यानं कुरु त्वं वीक्षणादिकम् ॥ 83 ॥
2.m: And union arises from longing, which comes from gazing. / Therefore, turn your longing, gazing, and the rest toward your wives.

2.s:
yadyevaṃ naiva kuruṣe madvaco dharmayantritam |
tadā lokavacoduṣṭaḥ pāpavāṃstvaṃ bhaviṣyasi || 84 ||
2.d:
यद्येवं नैव कुरुषे मद्वचो धर्मयन्त्रितम् ।
तदा लोकवचोदुष्टः पापवांस्त्वं भविष्यसि ॥ 84 ॥
2.m: If you do not act upon this word of mine, restrained by dharma, / then, ruined by worldly censure, you will become a sinner.”

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
etacchrutvā vacastasya dakṣasya sumahātmanaḥ |
evamastviti candro'pi nyagadaddakṣaśaṃkayā || 85 ||
2.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य दक्षस्य सुमहात्मनः ।
एवमस्त्विति चन्द्रोऽपि न्यगदद्दक्षशंकया ॥ 85 ॥
2.m: Hearing these words of the noble Dakṣa, / out of fear of Dakṣa, the Moon too said, “So be it.”

2.s:
athānumantrya tanayāścandraṃ jāmātāraṃ tathā |
yayo dakṣo nijaṃ sthānaṃ kṛtakṛtyastadā muniḥ || 86 ||
2.d:
अथानुमन्त्र्य तनयाश्चन्द्रं जामातारं तथा ।
ययो दक्षो निजं स्थानं कृतकृत्यस्तदा मुनिः ॥ 86 ॥
2.m: Then, having given counsel to his daughters and to his son-in-law, the Moon, / the sage Dakṣa, his task accomplished, went to his own abode.

2.s:
gate dakṣe tataścandrastāṃ samāsādya rohiṇīm |
jagrāha pūrvavadbhāvaṃ tāsu tasyāṃ ca rāgataḥ || 87 ||
2.d:
गते दक्षे ततश्चन्द्रस्तां समासाद्य रोहिणीम् ।
जग्राह पूर्ववद्भावं तासु तस्यां च रागतः ॥ 87 ॥
2.m: When Dakṣa had gone, the Moon approached Rohiṇī / and resumed his former disposition toward them and toward her out of passion.

2.s:
tatraiva rohiṇīṃ prāpya na kāścidapi vīkṣate |
rohiṇyāmeva vasate tatastāḥ kupitāḥ punaḥ || 88 ||
2.d:
तत्रैव रोहिणीं प्राप्य न काश्चिदपि वीक्षते ।
रोहिण्यामेव वसते ततस्ताः कुपिताः पुनः ॥ 88 ॥
2.m: Having obtained Rohiṇī alone, he did not look at any of the others; / he lived solely with Rohiṇī. Then they became angry once more.

2.s:
gatvā tāḥ pitaraṃ prāhurdaurbhāgyodvignamānasāḥ |
somo vasati nāsmāsu rohiṇīṃ bhajate sadā || 89 ||
2.d:
गत्वा ताः पितरं प्राहुर्दौर्भाग्योद्विग्नमानसाः ।
सोमो वसति नास्मासु रोहिणीं भजते सदा ॥ 89 ॥
2.m: Their minds distressed by misfortune, they went and said to their father: / “Soma does not dwell with us; he always attends upon Rohiṇī.

2.s: tavāpi nākarodvākyaṃ tasmānnaḥ śaraṇaṃ bhava || 90 ||
2.d: तवापि नाकरोद्वाक्यं तस्मान्नः शरणं भव ॥ 90 ॥
2.m: He did not heed even your words. Therefore, be our refuge!”

2.s:
udvega kopasaṃyukta uttasthau tatkṣaṇānmuniḥ |
jagāma manasā dhyāyan kartavyaṃ nikaṭaṃ vidhoḥ || 91 ||
2.d:
उद्वेग कोपसंयुक्त उत्तस्थौ तत्क्षणान्मुनिः ।
जगाम मनसा ध्यायन् कर्तव्यं निकटं विधोः ॥ 91 ॥
2.m: Filled with agitation and anger, the sage rose up at that very moment / and, meditating in his mind on what must be done, went near the Moon.

2.s:
upagamya tadā prāha vacaścandraṃ prajāpatiḥ |
samaṃ vartasva bhāryāsu vaiṣamyaṃ tvaṃ parityaja || 92 ||
2.d:
उपगम्य तदा प्राह वचश्चन्द्रं प्रजापतिः ।
समं वर्तस्व भार्यासु वैषम्यं त्वं परित्यज ॥ 92 ॥
2.m: Approaching him, Prajāpati then spoke these words to the Moon: / “Behave equally toward your wives; abandon partiality.

2.s:
na cedidaṃ vaco'smākaṃ maurkhyāt tvaṃmāvabudhyase |
dharmaśāstrātigāyāhaṃ śapsye tubhyaṃ niśāpate || 93 ||
2.d:
न चेदिदं वचोऽस्माकं मौर्ख्यात् त्वंमावबुध्यसे ।
धर्मशास्त्रातिगायाहं शप्स्ये तुभ्यं निशापते ॥ 93 ॥
2.m: If out of foolishness you do not heed this word of mine, / I shall curse you, O lord of the night, for transgressing the treatises on dharma.”

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
tato dakṣabhayāccandrastatkartuṃprati tatpuraḥ |
aṃgīcakārātibhayāt kāryamevaṃ muhustviti || 94 ||
2.d:
ततो दक्षभयाच्चन्द्रस्तत्कर्तुंप्रति तत्पुरः ।
अंगीचकारातिभयात् कार्यमेवं मुहुस्त्विति ॥ 94 ॥
2.m: Then, out of fear of Dakṣa, the Moon repeatedly agreed before him, / out of great terror, to do so, saying, “It shall be done.”

2.s:
samaṃ pravartanaṃ kartuṃ bhāryāsvaṃgīkṛte tataḥ |
vidhunā prayayau dakṣaḥ svasthānaṃ candrasammataḥ || 95 ||
2.d:
समं प्रवर्तनं कर्तुं भार्यास्वंगीकृते ततः ।
विधुना प्रययौ दक्षः स्वस्थानं चन्द्रसम्मतः ॥ 95 ॥
2.m: When the Moon had agreed to behave equally / toward his wives, Dakṣa, respected by the Moon, went to his own abode.

2.s:
gate dakṣe niśānātho rohiṇyāsahito bhṛśam |
ramamāṇo visasmāra dakṣasya vacanantu saḥ || 96 ||
2.d:
गते दक्षे निशानाथो रोहिण्यासहितो भृशम् ।
रममाणो विसस्मार दक्षस्य वचनन्तु सः ॥ 96 ॥
2.m: When Dakṣa had gone, the lord of the night, sporting intensely / with Rohiṇī, forgot Dakṣa’s words.

2.s:
sevamānāśca tāḥ sarvā aśvinādyā manoramāḥ |
nābhajaccandramāstāsu avajñāmeva cākarot || 97 ||
2.d:
सेवमानाश्च ताः सर्वा अश्विनाद्या मनोरमाः ।
नाभजच्चन्द्रमास्तासु अवज्ञामेव चाकरोत् ॥ 97 ॥
2.m: And though all those charming women beginning with Aśvinī served him, / the Moon did not attend upon them; rather, he showed them only disrespect.

2.s:
avajñātāstu tāḥ sarvāścandreṇa piturastikam |
gatvaivārtasvarāścārtā rudantyaścedamabruvan || 98 ||
2.d:
अवज्ञातास्तु ताः सर्वाश्चन्द्रेण पितुरस्तिकम् ।
गत्वैवार्तस्वराश्चार्ता रुदन्त्यश्चेदमब्रुवन् ॥ 98 ॥
2.m: Disrespected by the Moon, all of them went to their father's presence / with cries of distress, and weeping, they said this:

2.s:
nākarodvacanaṃ somastavāpi munisattama |
avajñāṃ kurute'māsu pūrvato'pyadhikaṃ sa ca || 99 ||
2.d:
नाकरोद्वचनं सोमस्तवापि मुनिसत्तम ।
अवज्ञां कुरुतेऽमासु पूर्वतोऽप्यधिकं स च ॥ 99 ॥
2.m: “Soma did not heed even your words, O best of sages. / He shows disrespect toward us even more than before.

2.s:
tasmāt somena naḥ kārya na kiṃcidapi vidyate |
tapasvinyo bhaviṣyāmastapaścaryā nideśaya || 100 ||
2.d:
तस्मात् सोमेन नः कार्य न किंचिदपि विद्यते ।
तपस्विन्यो भविष्यामस्तपश्चर्या निदेशय ॥ 100 ॥
2.m: Therefore, we have no business whatsoever with Soma. / We shall become female ascetics; assign us our ascetic practice!

2.s:
tapasā śodhitātmānaḥ parityakṣyāma jīvitam |
kimasmākaṃ jīvitena durbhagānāṃ dvijottama || 101 ||
2.d:
तपसा शोधितात्मानः परित्यक्ष्याम जीवितम् ।
किमस्माकं जीवितेन दुर्भगानां द्विजोत्तम ॥ 101 ॥
2.m: Purifying ourselves through asceticism, we shall abandon our lives. / What is the use of our lives, miserable as we are, O best of the twice-born?”

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
ityuktvā tāstataḥ sarvā dakṣajāḥ kṛttikādayaḥ |
kapolamālambya karairūrudurviviśuḥ kṣitau || 102 ||
2.d:
इत्युक्त्वा तास्ततः सर्वा दक्षजाः कृत्तिकादयः ।
कपोलमालम्ब्य करैरूरुदुर्विविशुः क्षितौ ॥ 102 ॥
2.m: Having spoken thus, all those daughters of Dakṣa beginning with Kṛttikā / rested their cheeks on their hands, wept, and sank to the ground.

2.s:
tāstu dṛṣṭvā tathābhūtā duḥkhavyākulitendriyāḥ |
atidīnamukho dakṣaḥ kopājjajvāla vahnivat || 103 ||
2.d:
तास्तु दृष्ट्वा तथाभूता दुःखव्याकुलितेन्द्रियाः ।
अतिदीनमुखो दक्षः कोपाज्जज्वाल वह्निवत् ॥ 103 ॥
2.m: Seeing them in such a state, their faculties perturbed by grief, / Dakṣa, his face showing extreme distress, blazed like fire with rage.

2.s:
atha kopaparītasya dakṣasya sumahātmanaḥ |
niścakrāma tadā yakṣmā nāsikāgrādvibhīṣaṇaḥ || 104 ||
2.d:
अथ कोपपरीतस्य दक्षस्य सुमहात्मनः ।
निश्चक्राम तदा यक्ष्मा नासिकाग्राद्विभीषणः ॥ 104 ॥
2.m: Then, from the tip of the nose of the noble Dakṣa, / filled with rage, emerged the terrifying Yakṣman [Consumption],

2.s:
daṃṣṭrākarālavadanaḥ kṛṣṇāṃgārasamaprabhaḥ |
atidīrghaḥ svalpakeśaḥ kṛśo ghamanisantataḥ || 105 ||
2.d:
दंष्ट्राकरालवदनः कृष्णांगारसमप्रभः ।
अतिदीर्घः स्वल्पकेशः कृशो घमनिसन्ततः ॥ 105 ॥
2.m: his mouth terrible with fangs, resembling black charcoal in luster, / very tall, with sparse hair, emaciated, his veins prominent,

2.s:
adhomukho daṇḍahastaḥ kāsaṃ viśramya santatam |
kurvāṇo nimnanetraśca yoṣāsambhogalolupaḥ || 106 ||
2.d:
अधोमुखो दण्डहस्तः कासं विश्रम्य सन्ततम् ।
कुर्वाणो निम्ननेत्रश्च योषासम्भोगलोलुपः ॥ 106 ॥
2.m: with face cast downward, a staff in hand, coughing incessantly without pause, / with sunken eyes, and lusting for the enjoyment of women.

2.s:
sa covāca tadā dakṣaṃ kasmiṃsthāsyāmyahaṃ mune |
kiṃvā cāhaṃ kariṣyāmi tanmevada mahāmate || 107 ||
2.d:
स चोवाच तदा दक्षं कस्मिंस्थास्याम्यहं मुने ।
किंवा चाहं करिष्यामि तन्मेवद महामते ॥ 107 ॥
2.m: He then said to Dakṣa: “In whom shall I dwell, O sage? / Or what shall I do? Tell me that, O noble-minded one.”

2.s:
tato dakṣastu taṃ prāha somaṃ yātu drutaṃ bhavān |
somamattu bhavānnityaṃ some tvaṃ tiṣṭha svecchayā || 108 ||
2.d:
ततो दक्षस्तु तं प्राह सोमं यातु द्रुतं भवान् ।
सोममत्तु भवान्नित्यं सोमे त्वं तिष्ठ स्वेच्छया ॥ 108 ॥
2.m: Then Dakṣa said to him: “Go swiftly to Soma! / Devour Soma continually; dwell in Soma at your will!”

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
iti śrutvā vacastasya dakṣasyātha mahāmuneḥ |
śanaiḥ śanaistataḥ somamāsasāda gadaḥ sa ca || 109 ||
2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य दक्षस्याथ महामुनेः ।
शनैः शनैस्ततः सोममाससाद गदः स च ॥ 109 ॥
2.m: Having heard those words of Dakṣa, the great sage, / that disease slowly approached Soma.

2.s:
āsādya sa tadā somaṃ vālmīkaṃ pannago yathā |
praviveśenduhṛdayaṃ chidraṃ prāpya mahāgadaḥ || 110 ||
2.d:
आसाद्य स तदा सोमं वाल्मीकं पन्नगो यथा ।
प्रविवेशेन्दुहृदयं छिद्रं प्राप्य महागदः ॥ 110 ॥
2.m: Approaching Soma then, like a snake entering an anthill, / that great disease, finding an opening, entered the moon’s heart.

2.s:
tasmin praviṣṭe hṛdaye dāruṇe rājayakṣmaṇi |
mumoha candrastandrāṃ ca viṣamāṃ prāptavāṃśca saḥ || 111 ||
2.d:
तस्मिन् प्रविष्टे हृदये दारुणे राजयक्ष्मणि ।
मुमोह चन्द्रस्तन्द्रां च विषमां प्राप्तवांश्च सः ॥ 111 ॥
2.m: When that dreadful consumption had entered his heart, / the moon lost consciousness and fell into a profound stupor.

2.s:
utpadya prathamaṃ yasmāllīno rājanyasau gadaḥ |
rājayakṣmeti loke'sminnasya khyātirabhūddvijāḥ || 112 ||
2.d:
उत्पद्य प्रथमं यस्माल्लीनो राजन्यसौ गदः ।
राजयक्ष्मेति लोकेऽस्मिन्नस्य ख्यातिरभूद्द्विजाः ॥ 112 ॥
2.m: Because this disease first arose and dissolved into the king, / it became known in this world as rājayakṣmā, O twice-born ones.

2.s:
tatastenābhibhūtaḥ sa yakṣmaṇā rohiṇīpatiḥ |
kṣayaṃ jagāmānudinaṃ grīṣme kṣudrā nadī yathā || 113 ||
2.d:
ततस्तेनाभिभूतः स यक्ष्मणा रोहिणीपतिः ।
क्षयं जगामानुदिनं ग्रीष्मे क्षुद्रा नदी यथा ॥ 113 ॥
2.m: Overcome then by that consumption, the husband of Rohiṇī / waned day by day, like a small stream in summer.

2.s:
atha candre kṣīyamāṇe sarvauṣadhyo gatā kṣayam |
kṣayaṃ yātāsvauṣadhiṣu na yajñaḥ samavartata || 114 ||
2.d:
अथ चन्द्रे क्षीयमाणे सर्वौषध्यो गता क्षयम् ।
क्षयं यातास्वौषधिषु न यज्ञः समवर्तत ॥ 114 ॥
2.m: Now, as the moon waned, all medicinal plants perished; / when the plants had perished, no sacrifice could proceed.

2.s:
yajñābhāvāttu devānāmannaṃ sarvaṃ kṣayaṃ gatam |
parjanyāśca tato naṣṭāstato vṛṣṭirnacābhavat || 115 ||
2.d:
यज्ञाभावात्तु देवानामन्नं सर्वं क्षयं गतम् ।
पर्जन्याश्च ततो नष्टास्ततो वृष्टिर्नचाभवत् ॥ 115 ॥
2.m: Because of the lack of sacrifice, all food of the gods was exhausted; / then the rain clouds vanished, and no rain fell.

2.s:
vṛṣṭyabhāve tu lokānāmāhārāḥ kṣīṇatāṃ gatāḥ
durbhikṣavyasanopete sarvaloke dvijottamāḥ || 116 ||
2.d:
वृष्ट्यभावे तु लोकानामाहाराः क्षीणतां गताः
दुर्भिक्षव्यसनोपेते सर्वलोके द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 116 ॥
2.m: In the absence of rain, the food of the creatures dwindled, / and when the entire world was afflicted by famine, O best of the twice-born,

2.s:
dānadharmādikaṃ kiṃcinna lokasya pravartate |
sattvahīnāḥ prajāḥ sarvā lobhenopahatendriyāḥ |
pāpameva tadā cakruḥ kukarmaratayaśca tāḥ || 117 ||
2.d:
दानधर्मादिकं किंचिन्न लोकस्य प्रवर्तते ।
सत्त्वहीनाः प्रजाः सर्वा लोभेनोपहतेन्द्रियाः ।
पापमेव तदा चक्रुः कुकर्मरतयश्च ताः ॥ 117 ॥
2.m: no acts of charity, righteousness, and the like took place among the people; / all creatures, bereft of vitality, their senses ruined by greed, / committed only sin and took pleasure in evil deeds.

2.s:
etān dṛṣṭvā tadā bhāvān dikpālāḥ sapurandarāḥ |
jagmuḥ kṣobhaṃ paraṃ devāḥ sāgarāśca grahāstathā || 118 ||
2.d:
एतान् दृष्ट्वा तदा भावान् दिक्पालाः सपुरन्दराः ।
जग्मुः क्षोभं परं देवाः सागराश्च ग्रहास्तथा ॥ 118 ॥
2.m: Seeing these occurrences, the guardians of the directions along with Purandara, / the gods, the oceans, and the planets were thrown into great agitation.

2.s:
tato dṛṣṭvā jagatsarvaṃ vyākulaṃ dasyupīḍitam |
brahmāṇamagaman devāḥ sarve śakrapurogamāḥ || 119 ||
2.d:
ततो दृष्ट्वा जगत्सर्वं व्याकुलं दस्युपीडितम् ।
ब्रह्माणमगमन् देवाः सर्वे शक्रपुरोगमाः ॥ 119 ॥
2.m: Then, seeing the whole world distraught and oppressed by robbers, / all the gods, led by Śakra, went to Brahmā.

2.s:
upasaṃgamya deveśaṃ sraṣṭāraṃ jagatāṃ patim |
praṇamyātha yathāyogyamupaviṣṭāstadā surāḥ || 120 ||
2.d:
उपसंगम्य देवेशं स्रष्टारं जगतां पतिम् ।
प्रणम्याथ यथायोग्यमुपविष्टास्तदा सुराः ॥ 120 ॥
2.m: Approaching the lord of gods, the creator, the master of the worlds, / and bowing low, the gods then sat down in a fitting manner.

2.s:
tān mlānavadanān sarvān vīkṣya lokapitāmahaḥ |
abhibhūtān pareṇeva hṛtasvaviṣayāniva |
papraccha sammukhīkṛtya gurumindraṃ hutāśanam || 121 ||
2.d:
तान् म्लानवदनान् सर्वान् वीक्ष्य लोकपितामहः ।
अभिभूतान् परेणेव हृतस्वविषयानिव ।
पप्रच्छ सम्मुखीकृत्य गुरुमिन्द्रं हुताशनम् ॥ 121 ॥
2.m: Seeing them all with withered faces, / as if overwhelmed by an enemy or stripped of their domains, / the grandfather of the worlds addressed Guru, Indra, and the Fire-god, and asked:

2.s: brahmovāca
2.d: ब्रह्मोवाच

2.s:
svāgata bho suragaṇāḥ kimarthaṃ yūyamāgatāḥ |
duḥkhopahatadehāṃśca yuṣmān mlānāṃśca lakṣaye || 122 ||
2.d:
स्वागत भो सुरगणाः किमर्थं यूयमागताः ।
दुःखोपहतदेहांश्च युष्मान् म्लानांश्च लक्षये ॥ 122 ॥
2.m: “Welcome, O hosts of gods! For what purpose have you come? / I see your bodies afflicted by sorrow and your spirits downcast.

2.s:
nirābādhānnirātaṃkān yuṣmān sarvāṃścaṃ kāmagān |
kṛtvā svaviṣaye nyastān kathaṃ paśyāmi duḥkhitān || 123 ||
2.d:
निराबाधान्निरातंकान् युष्मान् सर्वांश्चं कामगान् ।
कृत्वा स्वविषये न्यस्तान् कथं पश्यामि दुःखितान् ॥ 123 ॥
2.m: Having placed you in your respective domains, free from obstacle, / free from anxiety, going wherever you desire, how is it that I see you suffering?

2.s:
yadvo'bhavadduḥkhabījaṃ yuṣmān vā yastu bādhate |
tatkathyatāmaśeṣeṇa siddhañcāpyavadhāryatām || 124 ||
2.d:
यद्वोऽभवद्दुःखबीजं युष्मान् वा यस्तु बाधते ।
तत्कथ्यतामशेषेण सिद्धञ्चाप्यवधार्यताम् ॥ 124 ॥
2.m: Whatever root of sorrow has befallen you, or whoever oppresses you, / let that be told in full, and consider it already accomplished!”

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
tato vṛddhaśravā jīvaḥ kṛṣṇavartmā ca lokabhṛt |
uvācātmabhuve tasmai surāṇāṃ duḥkhakāraṇam || 125 ||
2.d:
ततो वृद्धश्रवा जीवः कृष्णवर्त्मा च लोकभृत् ।
उवाचात्मभुवे तस्मै सुराणां दुःखकारणम् ॥ 125 ॥
2.m: Then Vṛddhaśravas, Jīva, and the black-pathed Fire, upholder of the world, / told that self-born one the cause of the gods’ distress.

2.s:
devāḥ ūcuḥ
śṛṇu sarvaṃ jagatkartastvāṃ yena vayamāgatāḥ |
yadvāsmākaṃ duḥkhabījaṃ yato mlānaśriyo vayam || 126 ||
2.d:
देवाः ऊचुः
शृणु सर्वं जगत्कर्तस्त्वां येन वयमागताः ।
यद्वास्माकं दुःखबीजं यतो म्लानश्रियो वयम् ॥ 126 ॥
2.m:
The gods said:
“Hear all, O creator of the world, why we have come to you, / what the root of our sorrow is, and why our splendour is dimmed.

2.s:
na kvacit sampravartante yajñā loke pitāmaha |
nirādhārā nirātaṃkāḥ prajāḥ sarvā kṣayaṃ gatā || 127 ||
2.d:
न क्वचित् सम्प्रवर्तन्ते यज्ञा लोके पितामह ।
निराधारा निरातंकाः प्रजाः सर्वा क्षयं गता ॥ 127 ॥
2.m: Sacrifices are nowhere performed in the world, O grandfather; / supportless and helpless, all creatures have perished.

2.s:
na ca dānādidharmaśca na tapāṃsi kṣito kvacit |
naiva varṣati parjanyaḥ kṣīṇatoyābhavat kṣitiḥ || 128 ||
2.d:
न च दानादिधर्मश्च न तपांसि क्षितो क्वचित् ।
नैव वर्षति पर्जन्यः क्षीणतोयाभवत् क्षितिः ॥ 128 ॥
2.m: Nowhere on earth is there charity, righteousness, or asceticism; / the cloud does not rain, and the earth is depleted of water.

2.s:
kṣīṇāḥ sarvāstathauṣadhyaḥ śasyā lokāḥ samākulāḥ |
dasyubhiḥ pīḍitā viprā vedavādaṃ na kurvate || 129 ||
2.d:
क्षीणाः सर्वास्तथौषध्यः शस्या लोकाः समाकुलाः ।
दस्युभिः पीडिता विप्रा वेदवादं न कुर्वते ॥ 129 ॥
2.m: All medicinal plants and crops have withered, and the worlds are distressed; / oppressed by robbers, the brāhmaṇas do not recite the Vedas.

2.s:
annavaikalyamāsādya mriyante bahavaḥ prajāḥ |
kṣīṇeṣu yajñabhāgeṣu bhogyahīnāstathā vayam || 130 ||
2.d:
अन्नवैकल्यमासाद्य म्रियन्ते बहवः प्रजाः ।
क्षीणेषु यज्ञभागेषु भोग्यहीनास्तथा वयम् ॥ 130 ॥
2.m: Having met with a lack of food, many creatures are dying; / with sacrificial shares exhausted, we too are deprived of enjoyment.

2.s: durbalāstu śriyā hīnā naiva śānti labhāmahe || 131 ||
2.d: दुर्बलास्तु श्रिया हीना नैव शान्ति लभामहे ॥ 131 ॥
2.m: Weak and bereft of glory, we find no peace at all.

2.s:
rohiṇyā mandire candro vakragatyā ciraṃ sthitaḥ |
vṛṣarāśau sa ca kṣīṇo jyotsnāhīnaśca vartate || 132 ||
2.d:
रोहिण्या मन्दिरे चन्द्रो वक्रगत्या चिरं स्थितः ।
वृषराशौ स च क्षीणो ज्योत्स्नाहीनश्च वर्तते ॥ 132 ॥
2.m: The moon has stayed a long time in retrograde motion in the mansion of Rohiṇī; / he is diminished in the sign of Taurus and bereft of moonlight.

2.s:
yadaivānviṣyate devaiścandro naiṣā puraḥsaraḥ |
kadācidapi devānā samāje vā bhavadvidhe || 133 ||
2.d:
यदैवान्विष्यते देवैश्चन्द्रो नैषा पुरःसरः ।
कदाचिदपि देवाना समाजे वा भवद्विधे ॥ 133 ॥
2.m: Whenever the gods search for the moon, the night-maker, / even in an assembly of the gods such as yours,

2.s:
kadācidrohiṇī tyaktvā naiva kvacana gacchati |
yadyanya ko'pi na bhavettadā candro bahirbhavet || 134 ||
2.d:
कदाचिद्रोहिणी त्यक्त्वा नैव क्वचन गच्छति ।
यद्यन्य कोऽपि न भवेत्तदा चन्द्रो बहिर्भवेत् ॥ 134 ॥
2.m: he never abandons Rohiṇī to go anywhere else; / if no one else were present, only then might the moon come out.

2.s:
dṛśyate sa kalāhīnaḥ kalāmātrāvaśeṣakaḥ |
iti sarvatra lokeśa vṛttaḥ karmaviparyayaḥ || 135 ||
2.d:
दृश्यते स कलाहीनः कलामात्रावशेषकः ।
इति सर्वत्र लोकेश वृत्तः कर्मविपर्ययः ॥ 135 ॥
2.m: He is seen bereft of digits, with only a single digit remaining; / thus, O lord of the world, the course of actions has been overturned everywhere.

2.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā kāndiśīkāstu vayaṃ tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ |
pātālādyāvadutthāya kālakañjādayo'surāḥ || 136 ||
2.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा कान्दिशीकास्तु वयं त्वां शरणं गताः ।
पातालाद्यावदुत्थाय कालकञ्जादयोऽसुराः ॥ 136 ॥
2.m: Fleeing in panic upon seeing him, we have sought refuge in you; / before the asuras such as the Kālakañjas arise from Pātāla

2.s:
nāsmān lokeśa bādhante tāvannastrāhi sādhvasāt |
ayaṃ pravartate kasmājjagatāṃ vā vyatikramaḥ |
na jānīmastu tatsarvaṃ viplave vāpi kāraṇam || 137 ||
2.d:
नास्मान् लोकेश बाधन्ते तावन्नस्त्राहि साध्वसात् ।
अयं प्रवर्तते कस्माज्जगतां वा व्यतिक्रमः ।
न जानीमस्तु तत्सर्वं विप्लवे वापि कारणम् ॥ 137 ॥
2.m: and oppress us, O lord of the world, protect us from this terror! / Why this disorder of the worlds has arisen, / or the cause of this catastrophe, we do not know.”

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
etat surāṇāṃ vacanaṃ divyadarśī pitāmahaḥ |
śrutvā kṣaṇamabhidhyāyan nijagāda surottamān || 138 ||
2.d:
एतत् सुराणां वचनं दिव्यदर्शी पितामहः ।
श्रुत्वा क्षणमभिध्यायन् निजगाद सुरोत्तमान् ॥ 138 ॥
2.m: Hearing these words of the gods, the grandfather of divine vision / meditated for a moment and addressed the foremost of the gods.

2.s: brahmovāca
2.d: ब्रह्मोवाच

2.s:
śṛṇvantu devatāḥ sarvā yadarthaṃ lokaviplavaḥ |
pravartate'dhunā yena jñāntistasya bhaviṣyati || 139 ||
2.d:
शृण्वन्तु देवताः सर्वा यदर्थं लोकविप्लवः ।
प्रवर्ततेऽधुना येन ज्ञान्तिस्तस्य भविष्यति ॥ 139 ॥
2.m: “Let all the gods hear why this catastrophe of the world / is occurring now, by which knowledge of it will arise.

2.s:
somo dākṣāyaṇīḥ kanyāḥ saptaviṃśatisaṃkhyakāḥ |
aśvinyādyā varavadhūbhāryārthe pariṇītavān || 140 ||
2.d:
सोमो दाक्षायणीः कन्याः सप्तविंशतिसंख्यकाः ।
अश्विन्याद्या वरवधूभार्यार्थे परिणीतवान् ॥ 140 ॥
2.m: Soma took the daughters of Dakṣa, twenty-seven in number, / beginning with Aśvinī, excellent brides, to be his wives.

2.s:
pariṇīya sa tāḥ sarvā rohiṇyāṃ satataṃ vidhuḥ |
prāvartatānurāgeṇa na samastāsu vartate || 141 ||
2.d:
परिणीय स ताः सर्वा रोहिण्यां सततं विधुः ।
प्रावर्ततानुरागेण न समस्तासु वर्तते ॥ 141 ॥
2.m: Having married them all, the moon constantly devoted himself / with passion only to Rohiṇī, and did not behave equally toward them all.

2.s:
aśvinyādyāstu tāḥ sarvā daurbhāgyajvarapīḍitāḥ |
ṣaḍviṃśatirvarārohāḥ pitaraṃ prasthitāḥ svakam || 142 ||
2.d:
अश्विन्याद्यास्तु ताः सर्वा दौर्भाग्यज्वरपीडिताः ।
षड्विंशतिर्वरारोहाः पितरं प्रस्थिताः स्वकम् ॥ 142 ॥
2.m: All those [wives] beginning with Aśvinī, afflicted by the fever of misfortune, / twenty-six slender-waisted women, went to their father.

2.s:
pravartate niśānātho rohiṇyā rāgato yathā |
tathā na tāsu bhajate taddakṣāya nyavedayat || 143 ||
2.d:
प्रवर्तते निशानाथो रोहिण्या रागतो यथा ।
तथा न तासु भजते तद्दक्षाय न्यवेदयत् ॥ 143 ॥
2.m: As the lord of the night acts out of passion toward Rohiṇī, / he does not attend to them in that way: this they reported to Dakṣa.

2.s:
tato dakṣo mahābuddhiḥ sāmnā saṃstūya viṭpatim |
bahusunṛtamābhāṣya putryarthe cānvarodhata || 144 ||
2.d:
ततो दक्षो महाबुद्धिः साम्ना संस्तूय विट्पतिम् ।
बहुसुनृतमाभाष्य पुत्र्यर्थे चान्वरोधत ॥ 144 ॥
2.m: Then Dakṣa, of great intellect, soothing the lord of stars with conciliation / and speaking many pleasing words, urged him for the sake of his daughters.

2.s:
anuruddho yathākāmaṃ dakṣeṇa sumahātmanā |
samaṃ pravartituṃ tāsu samayaṃ kṛtavān vidhuḥ || 145 ||
2.d:
अनुरुद्धो यथाकामं दक्षेण सुमहात्मना ।
समं प्रवर्तितुं तासु समयं कृतवान् विधुः ॥ 145 ॥
2.m: Urged at will by the high-souled Dakṣa, / the moon made an agreement to behave equally toward them.

2.s:
samamaṃgīkṛte bhāva tāsu kartuṃ himāṃśunā |
svaṃ jagāma tataḥ sthānaṃ dakṣo'pi munisattamaḥ || 146 ||
2.d:
सममंगीकृते भाव तासु कर्तुं हिमांशुना ।
स्वं जगाम ततः स्थानं दक्षोऽपि मुनिसत्तमः ॥ 146 ॥
2.m: When the cool-rayed moon had agreed to show equal affection toward them, / Dakṣa, the best of sages, departed to his own abode.

2.s:
gate dakṣe muniśreṣṭhe vaiṣamyaṃ tāsu candramāḥ |
jahau na bhāvaṃ tāḥ śaśvat kupitāḥ pitaraṃ gatāḥ || 147 ||
2.d:
गते दक्षे मुनिश्रेष्ठे वैषम्यं तासु चन्द्रमाः ।
जहौ न भावं ताः शश्वत् कुपिताः पितरं गताः ॥ 147 ॥
2.m: When Dakṣa, the foremost of sages, had gone, the moon did not abandon / his partiality toward them; continually angered, they went to their father.

2.s:
tato dakṣaḥ punaścandramanurudhya sutāntare |
samāṃ vṛttiṃ pratiśrāvya vacanaṃ cedamabravīt || 148 ||
2.d:
ततो दक्षः पुनश्चन्द्रमनुरुध्य सुतान्तरे ।
समां वृत्तिं प्रतिश्राव्य वचनं चेदमब्रवीत् ॥ 148 ॥
2.m: Then Dakṣa again urged the moon in the matter of his daughters, / made him promise equal conduct, and spoke these words:

2.s:
na samaṃ vartate candra sarvāsvāsu bhavān yadi |
tadā śapsye tvahaṃ tubhyaṃ tasmāt kuru samaṃjasam || 149 ||
2.d:
न समं वर्तते चन्द्र सर्वास्वासु भवान् यदि ।
तदा शप्स्ये त्वहं तुभ्यं तस्मात् कुरु समंजसम् ॥ 149 ॥
2.m: ‘If you do not behave equally toward all of these, O Candramā, / then I shall curse you; therefore, act properly!’

2.s:
tato gate punarddakṣe na samaṃ vartate yadā |
tāsu candrastadā dakṣaṃ punargatvāṇuvan ruṣā || 150 ||
2.d:
ततो गते पुनर्द्दक्षे न समं वर्तते यदा ।
तासु चन्द्रस्तदा दक्षं पुनर्गत्वाणुवन् रुषा ॥ 150 ॥
2.m: Then, when Dakṣa had gone again and the moon still did not act equally / toward them, they went to Dakṣa again and spoke in anger.”

2.s:
na te vacaḥ satkurute naivāsmāsu pravartate |
vayaṃ tapaścariṣyāmaḥ sthāsyāmaśca tavāntike || 151 ||
2.d:
न ते वचः सत्कुरुते नैवास्मासु प्रवर्तते ।
वयं तपश्चरिष्यामः स्थास्यामश्च तवान्तिके ॥ 151 ॥
2.m: "He does not honor your word, nor does he dwell with us at all. / We will practice austerities and stay near you."

2.s:
tāsāmiti vacaḥ śrutvā kupitaḥ sa mahāmuniḥ |
kṣayāya candrasya punaḥ śāpāyatsukatāṃ gataḥ || 152 ||
2.d:
तासामिति वचः श्रुत्वा कुपितः स महामुनिः ।
क्षयाय चन्द्रस्य पुनः शापायत्सुकतां गतः ॥ 152 ॥
2.m: Hearing this speech of theirs, the great sage was enraged, / and again sought to curse the moon to wane.

2.s:
śāpāyodyuktamamanasaḥ kupitasya mahāmune |
kṣayo nāma mahārogo nāsikāgrādvinirgataḥ || 153 ||
2.d:
शापायोद्युक्तममनसः कुपितस्य महामुने ।
क्षयो नाम महारोगो नासिकाग्राद्विनिर्गतः ॥ 153 ॥
2.m: As the enraged great sage turned his mind to cursing, / the great disease called consumption issued from the tip of his nose.

2.s:
preṣitaḥ sa ca candrāya dakṣeṇa muninā tataḥ |
praviṣṭaśca tato dehe kṣayitastena candramāḥ || 154 ||
2.d:
प्रेषितः स च चन्द्राय दक्षेण मुनिना ततः ।
प्रविष्टश्च ततो देहे क्षयितस्तेन चन्द्रमाः ॥ 154 ॥
2.m: It was then sent against the moon by the sage Dakṣa; / entering into his body, it caused the moon to wane.

2.s:
kṣīṇe candre kṣayaṃ yātā jyotsnāstasya mahātmanaḥ |
kṣīṇāsu sarvajyotsnāsu sarvauṣadhyaḥ kṣayaṃ gatāḥ || 155 ||
2.d:
क्षीणे चन्द्रे क्षयं याता ज्योत्स्नास्तस्य महात्मनः ।
क्षीणासु सर्वज्योत्स्नासु सर्वौषध्यः क्षयं गताः ॥ 155 ॥
2.m: When the moon waned, the moonlight of that great-souled one waned away. / When all moonlight had waned, all medicinal plants perished.

2.s:
auṣadhyabhāvālloke'smin na yajñaḥ sampravartate |
yajñābhāvādanāvṛṣṭistataḥ sarvaprajākṣayaḥ || 156 ||
2.d:
औषध्यभावाल्लोकेऽस्मिन् न यज्ञः सम्प्रवर्तते ।
यज्ञाभावादनावृष्टिस्ततः सर्वप्रजाक्षयः ॥ 156 ॥
2.m: From the absence of plants, no sacrifice could proceed in this world. / From the absence of sacrifice came drought, and then the destruction of all creatures.

2.s:
yajñabhāgopabhogena hīnānāṃ bhavatāṃ tathā |
durbalatvaṃ samutpannaṃ vikāraśca svagocare || 157 ||
2.d:
यज्ञभागोपभोगेन हीनानां भवतां तथा ।
दुर्बलत्वं समुत्पन्नं विकारश्च स्वगोचरे ॥ 157 ॥
2.m: Deprived likewise of the enjoyment of your sacrificial shares, / weakness arose in you, and disorder in your own realm.

2.s:
iti vaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ yathābhūllokaviplavaḥ |
yenopāyena tacchāntistacchṛṇvantu surottamāḥ || 158 ||
2.d:
इति वः कथितं सर्वं यथाभूल्लोकविप्लवः ।
येनोपायेन तच्छान्तिस्तच्छृण्वन्तु सुरोत्तमाः ॥ 158 ॥
2.m: Thus all has been related to you, how the ruin of the world occurred. / Hear now, O best of gods, the means by which its pacification [may be achieved].

2.s:
iti śrīkālikāpurāṇe candrasyaśāpa mokṣe viṃśo'dhyāyaḥ
ekaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ
2.d:
इति श्रीकालिकापुराणे चन्द्रस्यशाप मोक्षे विंशोऽध्यायः
एकविंशोऽध्यायः
2.m: Thus ends the twentieth chapter, on the release of the moon from the curse, [and begins] the twenty-first chapter in the glorious Kālikāpurāṇa.

2.s: brahmovāca
2.d: ब्रह्मोवाच

2.s:
gacchantu bhoḥ suragaṇā dakṣasya sadanaṃ prati |
prasādayatacandrārthe sa ca pūrṇo bhavedyathā || 1 ||
2.d:
गच्छन्तु भोः सुरगणा दक्षस्य सदनं प्रति ।
प्रसादयतचन्द्रार्थे स च पूर्णो भवेद्यथा ॥ 1 ॥
2.m: "Go, O hosts of gods, to Dakṣa's abode, / and propitiate [him] for the sake of the moon, so that he may become full.

2.s:
pūrṇe candre jagatsarvaṃ prakṛtisthaṃ bhaviṣyati |
yuṣmākañca bhavecchāntiroṣadhīṃnāñcasambhavaḥ || 2 ||
2.d:
पूर्णे चन्द्रे जगत्सर्वं प्रकृतिस्थं भविष्यति ।
युष्माकञ्च भवेच्छान्तिरोषधींनाञ्चसम्भवः ॥ 2 ॥
2.m: When the moon is full, the entire universe will be restored to its natural state; / you will have peace, and the medicinal plants will come into being."

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
iti brahmavacaḥ śrutvā devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ |
prayayurhṛṣṭha manasastadā dakṣaniveśanam || 3 ||
2.d:
इति ब्रह्मवचः श्रुत्वा देवाः शक्रपुरोगमाः ।
प्रययुर्हृष्ठ मनसस्तदा दक्षनिवेशनम् ॥ 3 ॥
2.m: Hearing these words of Brahmā, the gods, led by Śakra, / their minds delighted, then went to Dakṣa's residence.

2.s:
yathānyāyamupasthāya sarve munivaraṃ surāḥ |
procuḥ prajāpatiṃ dakṣaṃ praṇamya ślakṣṇayā girā || 4 ||
2.d:
यथान्यायमुपस्थाय सर्वे मुनिवरं सुराः ।
प्रोचुः प्रजापतिं दक्षं प्रणम्य श्लक्ष्णया गिरा ॥ 4 ॥
2.m: Approaching the best of sages according to rule, all the gods / bowed down and spoke to Dakṣa Prajāpati in gentle speech:

2.s: devā ūcuḥ
2.d: देवा ऊचुः

2.s:
prasīda sīdatāṃ brahmannasmākaṃ bahuduḥkhinām |
uddharasva mahābuddhe trāhi naḥ śokasāgarāt || 5 ||
2.d:
प्रसीद सीदतां ब्रह्मन्नस्माकं बहुदुःखिनाम् ।
उद्धरस्व महाबुद्धे त्राहि नः शोकसागरात् ॥ 5 ॥
2.m: "Be gracious, O Brahman, to us who are sinking in great sorrow! / Lift us up, O one of great wisdom; save us from the ocean of grief!

2.s:
yadrūpaṃ brahmasaṃjñantu sṛṣṭikṛt paramātmanaḥ |
tadaṃśastvaṃ paraṃ jyotirviprarūpa namo'stute || 6 ||
2.d:
यद्रूपं ब्रह्मसंज्ञन्तु सृष्टिकृत् परमात्मनः ।
तदंशस्त्वं परं ज्योतिर्विप्ररूप नमोऽस्तुते ॥ 6 ॥
2.m: The form known as Brahman that creates the universe belongs to the Supreme Self; / you are his portion, supreme light in the form of a brāhmaṇa: homage to you!

2.s:
rakṣaṇāt sarvajagatāṃ prajāpālanakāraṇāt |
dakṣaḥ prajāpatiśceti yogeśastaṃ numo vayam || 7 ||
2.d:
रक्षणात् सर्वजगतां प्रजापालनकारणात् ।
दक्षः प्रजापतिश्चेति योगेशस्तं नुमो वयम् ॥ 7 ॥
2.m: Because of protecting all the worlds and maintaining creatures, / [you are] Dakṣa and Prajāpati; we bow to him, the lord of yoga.

2.s:
dakṣāya sarvajagatāṃ dakṣāya kuśalātmanām |
dakṣāyātmahitāyāśu namastubhyaṃ mahātmane || 8 ||
2.d:
दक्षाय सर्वजगतां दक्षाय कुशलात्मनाम् ।
दक्षायात्महितायाशु नमस्तुभ्यं महात्मने ॥ 8 ॥
2.m: To the capable one of all the worlds, the capable one of skillful souls, / the capable one for his own welfare: homage at once to you, the great-souled one!

2.s:
satataṃ cintyamānasya yogibhirniyatendriyaiḥ |
sārasya sārabhūtastvaṃ dakṣāya paramātmane || 9 ||
2.d:
सततं चिन्त्यमानस्य योगिभिर्नियतेन्द्रियैः ।
सारस्य सारभूतस्त्वं दक्षाय परमात्मने ॥ 9 ॥
2.m: You are the essence of the essence constantly meditated upon / by yogins with subdued senses: [homage] to Dakṣa, the Supreme Self!

2.s:
yogivṛttiranādhṛṣya pāragāṇāṃ parāyaṇaḥ |
ādyantamuktaḥ sāhasā tasmai nityaṃ namo namaḥ || 10 ||
2.d:
योगिवृत्तिरनाधृष्य पारगाणां परायणः ।
आद्यन्तमुक्तः साहसा तस्मै नित्यं नमो नमः ॥ 10 ॥
2.m: Abiding in yoga, unassailable, the refuge of those who cross over, / free from beginning and end with courage: homage, homage ever to him!"

2.s:
iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā dakṣo yajñabhujāṃ tathā |
prāha prasannavadanaḥ śakramābhāṣya mukhyataḥ || 11 ||
2.d:
इति तेषां वचः श्रुत्वा दक्षो यज्ञभुजां तथा ।
प्राह प्रसन्नवदनः शक्रमाभाष्य मुख्यतः ॥ 11 ॥
2.m: Hearing these words of theirs, of those who enjoy the sacrifice, / Dakṣa, with a cheerful face, spoke, addressing Śakra first:

2.s: dakṣa uvāca
2.d: दक्ष उवाच

2.s:
kutaḥ śakra mahābāho bhavatāṃ duḥkhamāgatam |
duḥkhahetuṃ vada vibho śrotumicchāmyahantu tam || 12 ||
2.d:
कुतः शक्र महाबाहो भवतां दुःखमागतम् ।
दुःखहेतुं वद विभो श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहन्तु तम् ॥ 12 ॥
2.m: "Whence has this distress come upon you, O mighty-armed Śakra? / Tell me the cause of your distress, O lord; I wish to hear it.

2.s:
mamāsti vā kiṃ kartavyaṃ bhavatāṃ duḥkhahānaye |
tadahaṃ yadi śaknomi kariṣyāmi hitaṃ samam || 13 ||
2.d:
ममास्ति वा किं कर्तव्यं भवतां दुःखहानये ।
तदहं यदि शक्नोमि करिष्यामि हितं समम् ॥ 13 ॥
2.m: Or what ought I to do for the removal of your distress? / If I am able, I shall do what is beneficial and proper."

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya brahmasūnormahātmanaḥ |
jagāda vākpatiḥ śakro vītihotro'tha taṃ munim || 14 ||
2.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य ब्रह्मसूनोर्महात्मनः ।
जगाद वाक्पतिः शक्रो वीतिहोत्रोऽथ तं मुनिम् ॥ 14 ॥
2.m: Hearing these words of that great-souled son of Brahmā, / the lord of speech, Śakra, and Vītihotra then addressed that sage.

2.s: ta ūcu
2.d: त ऊचु

2.s:
kṣayī jāto niśānāthastasmin kṣīṇe kṣayaṃ gatāḥ |
sarvauṣadhyo dvijaśreṣṭha taddhāniryajñahānikṛt || 15 ||
2.d:
क्षयी जातो निशानाथस्तस्मिन् क्षीणे क्षयं गताः ।
सर्वौषध्यो द्विजश्रेष्ठ तद्धानिर्यज्ञहानिकृत् ॥ 15 ॥
2.m: "The lord of night has become consumptive; when he waned, all medicinal plants / perished, O best of the twice-born; that loss causes the loss of sacrifices.

2.s:
yajñe vinaṣṭe sakalāḥ prajāḥ kṣudbhayakātarāḥ |
vṛṣṭyabhavānmahadduḥkhaṃ prāpya naṣṭāśca kāścana || 16 ||
2.d:
यज्ञे विनष्टे सकलाः प्रजाः क्षुद्भयकातराः ।
वृष्ट्यभवान्महद्दुःखं प्राप्य नष्टाश्च काश्चन ॥ 16 ॥
2.m: When sacrifice is destroyed, all creatures are afflicted with the dread of hunger; / suffering great misery from lack of rain, some have perished.

2.s:
kṣayo'yaṃ rātrināthasya yaste kopāt pravartate |
sa sarvajagato brahmannabhāvārthamupasthitaḥ || 17 ||
2.d:
क्षयोऽयं रात्रिनाथस्य यस्ते कोपात् प्रवर्तते ।
स सर्वजगतो ब्रह्मन्नभावार्थमुपस्थितः ॥ 17 ॥
2.m: This consumption of the lord of night, which proceeds from your anger, / has arrived for the destruction of the entire universe, O Brahman.

2.s:
nādhunā tat tribhuvana yanna kṣubdhaṃ nu kiṃcana |
viplutaṃ vāsti viprendra sthāvarā patagāśca vā || 18 ||
2.d:
नाधुना तत् त्रिभुवन यन्न क्षुब्धं नु किंचन ।
विप्लुतं वास्ति विप्रेन्द्र स्थावरा पतगाश्च वा ॥ 18 ॥
2.m: There is nothing in the three worlds now that is not agitated / or afflicted, O best of brāhmaṇas, whether stationary beings or birds.

2.s:
na yajñāḥ saṃpravartante na tapasyanti tāpasāḥ |
āhāraduḥkhānniśrīkāḥ prajāḥ kṣīṇā bhayāturāḥ || 19 ||
2.d:
न यज्ञाः संप्रवर्तन्ते न तपस्यन्ति तापसाः ।
आहारदुःखान्निश्रीकाः प्रजाः क्षीणा भयातुराः ॥ 19 ॥
2.m: No sacrifices are performed; ascetics do not practice penance; / creatures, stripped of splendor from the pain of lack of food, are emaciated and stricken with fear.

2.s:
evaṃ pravṛtte viprendra viplave'smāt rasātalām |
daityā na yāvadutthāya bādhante tāvaduddhara || 20 ||
2.d:
एवं प्रवृत्ते विप्रेन्द्र विप्लवेऽस्मात् रसातलाम् ।
दैत्या न यावदुत्थाय बाधन्ते तावदुद्धर ॥ 20 ॥
2.m: While such ruin proceeds, O best of brāhmaṇas, deliver [us] / before the Daityas rise up from the netherworld and harass [us]!

2.s:
prasīda dakṣa candrasaya taṃ pūraya tapobalāt |
pūrṇe candre jagatsarvaṃ prakṛtisthaṃ bhaviṣyati || 21 ||
2.d:
प्रसीद दक्ष चन्द्रसय तं पूरय तपोबलात् ।
पूर्णे चन्द्रे जगत्सर्वं प्रकृतिस्थं भविष्यति ॥ 21 ॥
2.m: Be gracious to the moon, O Dakṣa; make him full by the power of your penance! / When the moon is full, the entire universe will be restored to its natural state."

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā prajāpatisutastadā |
uvāca tān suragaṇān hṛdayācchalyamuddharan || 22 ||
2.d:
इति तेषां वचः श्रुत्वा प्रजापतिसुतस्तदा ।
उवाच तान् सुरगणान् हृदयाच्छल्यमुद्धरन् ॥ 22 ॥
2.m: Hearing this speech of theirs, the son of Prajāpati then / spoke to those hosts of gods, removing the dart from their heart:

2.s: dakṣa uvāca
2.d: दक्ष उवाच

2.s:
yanme vaco niśānāthe pravṛttaṃ śāpakāraṇam |
na kenāpi nidānena mithyā kartuṃ tadutsahe || 23 ||
2.d:
यन्मे वचो निशानाथे प्रवृत्तं शापकारणम् ।
न केनापि निदानेन मिथ्या कर्तुं तदुत्सहे ॥ 23 ॥
2.m: "The word that went forth from me against the lord of night, causing the curse, / I cannot venture to make false by any means whatsoever.

2.s:
kintu madvacanaṃ yasmānnaikāntena mṛṣā bhavet |
candro'pi vardhate yasmāttadupāyamudaikṣata || 24 ||
2.d:
किन्तु मद्वचनं यस्मान्नैकान्तेन मृषा भवेत् ।
चन्द्रोऽपि वर्धते यस्मात्तदुपायमुदैक्षत ॥ 24 ॥
2.m: Yet look upon a means whereby my word may not be completely false, / and the moon also may wax.

2.s:
tatrāpyayamupāyo'sti māsārdhaṃ yātu candramā |
kṣayaṃ vṛddhiñca māsārdhaṃ samaṃ bhāryāsu vartatām || 25 ||
2.d:
तत्राप्ययमुपायोऽस्ति मासार्धं यातु चन्द्रमा ।
क्षयं वृद्धिञ्च मासार्धं समं भार्यासु वर्तताम् ॥ 25 ॥
2.m: In that matter there is this means: let the moon undergo / waning for half a month and waxing for half a month, and let him dwell equally among his wives."

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā taṃ prasādya prajāpatim |
sarve suragaṇāstatra gatā yatāsti candramāḥ || 26 ||
2.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा तं प्रसाद्य प्रजापतिम् ।
सर्वे सुरगणास्तत्र गता यतास्ति चन्द्रमाः ॥ 26 ॥
2.m: Hearing those words of his and propitiating that Prajāpati, / all the hosts of gods went there where the moon was.

2.s:
evamukte tu vacane dakṣeṇa muninā dvijāḥ |
atha candraṃ samādāya bhāryābhiḥ sahitaṃ tadā |
jagmuste brahmabhavanaṃ muditāḥ surasattamāḥ || 27 ||
2.d:
एवमुक्ते तु वचने दक्षेण मुनिना द्विजाः ।
अथ चन्द्रं समादाय भार्याभिः सहितं तदा ।
जग्मुस्ते ब्रह्मभवनं मुदिताः सुरसत्तमाः ॥ 27 ॥
2.m: When those words had been spoken by the sage Dakṣa, O twice-born ones, / those best of gods, taking the moon along with his wives, / then went rejoiced to the abode of Brahmā.

2.s:
tatra gatvā mahābhāgā yathā dakṣeṇa bhāṣitam |
tatsarvaṃ kathayāmāsurbrahmaṇe paramātmane || 28 ||
2.d:
तत्र गत्वा महाभागा यथा दक्षेण भाषितम् ।
तत्सर्वं कथयामासुर्ब्रह्मणे परमात्मने ॥ 28 ॥
2.m: Having gone there, those fortunate ones related everything / that Dakṣa had spoken to Brahmā, the Supreme Self.

2.s:
brahma dakṣavacaḥ śrutvā devānāṃ vacanāttadā |
candrabhāgaṃ mahāśailaṃ jagāma sahitaḥ suraiḥ || 29 ||
2.d:
ब्रह्म दक्षवचः श्रुत्वा देवानां वचनात्तदा ।
चन्द्रभागं महाशैलं जगाम सहितः सुरैः ॥ 29 ॥
2.m: Having heard Dakṣa's words then from the speech of the gods, / Brahmā went with the gods to the great mountain Candrabhāga.

2.s:
tatra gatvā suraśreṣṭhaḥ prajānāṃ hitakāmyayā |
snāpayāmāsa śubhrāṃśuṃ vṛhallohitapuṣkare || 30 ||
2.d:
तत्र गत्वा सुरश्रेष्ठः प्रजानां हितकाम्यया ।
स्नापयामास शुभ्रांशुं वृहल्लोहितपुष्करे ॥ 30 ॥
2.m: Having gone there, the best of the gods, desiring the welfare of creatures, / bathed the bright-rayed [moon] in the Vṛhallohita lake.

2.s:
bhūtabhavyabhavajjñānaḥ pūrvameva pitāmahaḥ |
etadarthañcakārātra saraḥpūrṇaṃ jagadguruḥ || 31 ||
2.d:
भूतभव्यभवज्ज्ञानः पूर्वमेव पितामहः ।
एतदर्थञ्चकारात्र सरःपूर्णं जगद्गुरुः ॥ 31 ॥
2.m: Possessing knowledge of past, present, and future, the Grandfather, / the teacher of the world, had previously filled a lake here for this very purpose.

2.s:
tatra snātasya jantostu nīrogatvaṃ prajāyate |
cirāyuṣṭvañca satataṃ vṛhallohitasaṃjñake || 32 ||
2.d:
तत्र स्नातस्य जन्तोस्तु नीरोगत्वं प्रजायते ।
चिरायुष्ट्वञ्च सततं वृहल्लोहितसंज्ञके ॥ 32 ॥
2.m: When a living being bathes there in that [lake] called Vṛhallohita, / freedom from disease arises and long life forever.

2.s:
tatra snātasya candrasya śarīrāttatkṣaṇaṃ gadaḥ |
rājayakṣmā niḥsasāra pūrvarūpau yathoditaḥ || 33 ||
2.d:
तत्र स्नातस्य चन्द्रस्य शरीरात्तत्क्षणं गदः ।
राजयक्ष्मा निःससार पूर्वरूपौ यथोदितः ॥ 33 ॥
2.m: When the moon bathed there, the disease consumption, / as described in its preliminary form, immediately departed from his body.

2.s: rājayakṣmā uvāca
2.d: राजयक्ष्मा उवाच

2.s:
niḥsṛtya rājayakṣmāpi brahmāṇañca jagatpatim |
praṇamyāhaṃ kiṃ kariṣye kva gacchāmītyuvāca tam || 34 ||
2.d:
निःसृत्य राजयक्ष्मापि ब्रह्माणञ्च जगत्पतिम् ।
प्रणम्याहं किं करिष्ये क्व गच्छामीत्युवाच तम् ॥ 34 ॥
2.m: Having come forth, consumption too bowed down to Brahmā, the lord of the world, / and said to him: "What shall I do? Where shall I go?"

2.s:
sthānaṃ patnīñca lokeśa kṛtyaṃ mama sanātanam |
nideśayānurūpaṃ me sraṣṭā tvaṃ jagatāṃ yataḥ || 35 ||
2.d:
स्थानं पत्नीञ्च लोकेश कृत्यं मम सनातनम् ।
निदेशयानुरूपं मे स्रष्टा त्वं जगतां यतः ॥ 35 ॥
2.m: "O Lord of the worlds, designate a dwelling, a wife, / and my eternal duty suited to me, for you are the creator of the worlds."

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
tato brahmāpi taṃ puṣṭaṃ nirīkṣyenduṃ śarīragaiḥ |
amṛtaistenātiyuktaiḥ kṣīṇañcāpi niśāpatim || 36 ||
2.d:
ततो ब्रह्मापि तं पुष्टं निरीक्ष्येन्दुं शरीरगैः ।
अमृतैस्तेनातियुक्तैः क्षीणञ्चापि निशापतिम् ॥ 36 ॥
2.m: Then Brahmā, seeing that the moon was swollen with the ambrosia / belonging to the body now excessively attached to him, and that the lord of the night was also emaciated,

2.s:
dorbhiḥ svayaṃ tvaṃ gṛhītvā girau niṣpīḍya vai muhuḥ |
amṛtaṃ gālayāmāsa śarīrādrājayakṣmaṇaḥ || 37 ||
2.d:
दोर्भिः स्वयं त्वं गृहीत्वा गिरौ निष्पीड्य वै मुहुः ।
अमृतं गालयामास शरीराद्राजयक्ष्मणः ॥ 37 ॥
2.m: personally grasped him with his arms and, pressing repeatedly on the mountain, / squeezed out the ambrosia from the body of consumption.

2.s:
amṛtāni ca yānyāśu galitāni tadā jale |
kṣīrodasya sa cikṣepa madhye rahasi lokabhṛt || 38 ||
2.d:
अमृतानि च यान्याशु गलितानि तदा जले ।
क्षीरोदस्य स चिक्षेप मध्ये रहसि लोकभृत् ॥ 38 ॥
2.m: And the portions of ambrosia that quickly dripped down into the water, / the sustainer of the world cast secretly into the midst of the Ocean of Milk.

2.s:
tasmādasyāmṛtādindi kalāḥ kṣīṇāstu yāḥ purā |
tāsāṃ jagrāha lavaśaścūrṇān kṣīrodasāgarāt || 39 ||
2.d:
तस्मादस्यामृतादिन्दि कलाः क्षीणास्तु याः पुरा ।
तासां जग्राह लवशश्चूर्णान् क्षीरोदसागरात् ॥ 39 ॥
2.m: From that ambrosia of his, [as for] the digits that had previously waned, / he gathered up their powders, bit by bit, from the Ocean of Milk.

2.s:
kalāmātrāvaśeṣaṣya saṃsargādrājayakṣmaṇaḥ |
kṣīṇāḥ kalāḥ paṃcadaśa yāḥ pūrvamamṛtātmikāḥ || 40 ||
2.d:
कलामात्रावशेषष्य संसर्गाद्राजयक्ष्मणः ।
क्षीणाः कलाः पंचदश याः पूर्वममृतात्मिकाः ॥ 40 ॥
2.m: Of him who had only a single digit remaining, through contact with consumption, / the fifteen digits which were formerly of the nature of ambrosia had waned.

2.s:
tā rājayakṣmagarbhasthāścūrṇībhūtāstu pīḍayā |
tejojyotsnā sudhābhistu nibaddhaṃ yat kalāpateḥ || 41 ||
2.d:
ता राजयक्ष्मगर्भस्थाश्चूर्णीभूतास्तु पीडया ।
तेजोज्योत्स्ना सुधाभिस्तु निबद्धं यत् कलापतेः ॥ 41 ॥
2.m: Being inside the belly of consumption, they were reduced to powder under pressure. / The body of the lord of digits, which was composed of

2.s: śarīraṃ tat tridhā bhūtaṃ garbhasthaṃ rājayakṣmaṇaḥ || 42 ||
2.d: शरीरं तत् त्रिधा भूतं गर्भस्थं राजयक्ष्मणः ॥ 42 ॥
2.m: radiance, moonlight, and nectar, was divided into three inside the belly of consumption.

2.s:
jyotiścūrṇamabhūt jyotsnā līnā rājādiyakṣmaṇi |
dravībhūtāḥ sudhāḥ sarvāḥ garbhe rogasya ca sthitāḥ || 43 ||
2.d:
ज्योतिश्चूर्णमभूत् ज्योत्स्ना लीना राजादियक्ष्मणि ।
द्रवीभूताः सुधाः सर्वाः गर्भे रोगस्य च स्थिताः ॥ 43 ॥
2.m: The radiance became powder, the moonlight dissolved into consumption, / and all the nectars turned liquid and remained in the disease's belly.

2.s:
yadā nirgālayāmāsa sudhāṃ brahmā yakṣmāntarāt |
tadā jyotsnāsudhājyotiḥ sarvaṃ tasmādvahirgatam || 44 ||
2.d:
यदा निर्गालयामास सुधां ब्रह्मा यक्ष्मान्तरात् ।
तदा ज्योत्स्नासुधाज्योतिः सर्वं तस्माद्वहिर्गतम् ॥ 44 ॥
2.m: When Brahmā pressed out the nectar from inside consumption, / then moonlight, nectar, and radiance all came out of him.

2.s:
kṣīrodasāgare kṣiptaṃ tat sarvaṃ vidhinā tadā |
devān girau parityajya svayaṃ gatvā drutaṃ tataḥ || 45 ||
2.d:
क्षीरोदसागरे क्षिप्तं तत् सर्वं विधिना तदा ।
देवान् गिरौ परित्यज्य स्वयं गत्वा द्रुतं ततः ॥ 45 ॥
2.m: All that was cast into the Ocean of Milk by Vidhi then, / having left the gods on the mountain and gone swiftly there himself.

2.s:
tato'mṛtāni prakṣālya kalācūrṇāni vāribhiḥ |
jyotsnāñcāpyājagāmāśu gṛhītvā tattrayaṃ girim || 46 ||
2.d:
ततोऽमृतानि प्रक्षाल्य कलाचूर्णानि वारिभिः ।
ज्योत्स्नाञ्चाप्याजगामाशु गृहीत्वा तत्त्रयं गिरिम् ॥ 46 ॥
2.m: Then, having washed the ambrosias and the powder of the digits with water, / and taking that triad along with the moonlight, he quickly returned to the mountain.

2.s:
kṣīrodādgirimāsādya candrabhāgaṃ tadā vidhiḥ |
devamadhye kalācūrṇa sudhājyotsnā nyavīviśat || 47 ||
2.d:
क्षीरोदाद्गिरिमासाद्य चन्द्रभागं तदा विधिः ।
देवमध्ये कलाचूर्ण सुधाज्योत्स्ना न्यवीविशत् ॥ 47 ॥
2.m: Reaching the mountain from the Ocean of Milk, Vidhi then, / amidst the gods, inserted the portion of the moon—the powder of the digits, nectar, and moonlight.

2.s:
saṃsthāpya tattraya brahmā devānā madhyataḥ sthitaḥ |
jagāda rājayakṣmāṇa tat sthānādi nideśayan || 48 ||
2.d:
संस्थाप्य तत्त्रय ब्रह्मा देवाना मध्यतः स्थितः ।
जगाद राजयक्ष्माण तत् स्थानादि निदेशयन् ॥ 48 ॥
2.m: Having placed that triad and standing in the midst of the gods, / Brahmā spoke to consumption, designating its dwelling and the like.

2.s: brahmovāca
2.d: ब्रह्मोवाच

2.s:
sarvadā yo divārātra sandhyāyāṃ vanitārataḥ |
sevate surata tasmin rājayakṣman vasiṣyasi || 49 ||
2.d:
सर्वदा यो दिवारात्र सन्ध्यायां वनितारतः ।
सेवते सुरत तस्मिन् राजयक्ष्मन् वसिष्यसि ॥ 49 ॥
2.m: "He who is always devoted to women day and night, at twilight, / and indulges in sexual intercourse—in him, O consumption, you shall dwell.

2.s:
pratiśyāya-śvāsakāsa-sayukto maithuna caret |
sa te praveśya satata śleṣmaṇaśca tathāvidhaḥ || 50 ||
2.d:
प्रतिश्याय-श्वासकास-सयुक्तो मैथुन चरेत् ।
स ते प्रवेश्य सतत श्लेष्मणश्च तथाविधः ॥ 50 ॥
2.m: He who, afflicted with catarrh, asthma, and cough, engages in intercourse— / he, having phlegm of such a kind, is always to be entered by you.

2.s:
kṛṣṇākhyā mṛtyuputrī yā bhavataḥ sadṛśī guṇaiḥ |
sā te'stu bhāryā satataṃ bhavantamanuyāsyati || 51 ||
2.d:
कृष्णाख्या मृत्युपुत्री या भवतः सदृशी गुणैः ।
सा तेऽस्तु भार्या सततं भवन्तमनुयास्यति ॥ 51 ॥
2.m: The daughter of Death named Kṛṣṇā, who equals you in qualities, / shall be your wife; she will always accompany you.

2.s:
kṣīṇatvaṃ bhavataḥ kṛtyaṃ tatastvaṃ viṣayaṃ kuru |
drutaṃ gaccha yathākāmaṃ candrāt tvaṃ vimukho bhava || 52 ||
2.d:
क्षीणत्वं भवतः कृत्यं ततस्त्वं विषयं कुरु ।
द्रुतं गच्छ यथाकामं चन्द्रात् त्वं विमुखो भव ॥ 52 ॥
2.m: Causing emaciation is your duty; therefore, make it your realm. / Go swiftly where you will; turn away from the moon."

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
evaṃ visṛṣṭo vidhinā rājayakṣmā mahāgadaḥ |
paśyatāṃ arvadevānāmantardhānaṃ jagāma ha || 53 ||
2.d:
एवं विसृष्टो विधिना राजयक्ष्मा महागदः ।
पश्यतां अर्वदेवानामन्तर्धानं जगाम ह ॥ 53 ॥
2.m: Dismissed thus by Vidhi, consumption, the great disease, / vanished before the eyes of all the gods.

2.s:
antarhite mahāroge brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ |
candraṃ samagrayāmāsa kalāpañcadaśaidhitam || 54 ||
2.d:
अन्तर्हिते महारोगे ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ।
चन्द्रं समग्रयामास कलापञ्चदशैधितम् ॥ 54 ॥
2.m: When the great disease had vanished, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / restored the moon to wholeness, increased by fifteen digits.

2.s:
tena kṣīrodadhautena sudhāpūtena cātmabhūḥ |
sajyotsnaistu kalācūrṇaiḥ pūrvavaccākarodvidhum || 55 ||
2.d:
तेन क्षीरोदधौतेन सुधापूतेन चात्मभूः ।
सज्योत्स्नैस्तु कलाचूर्णैः पूर्ववच्चाकरोद्विधुम् ॥ 55 ॥
2.m: With that [powder] washed by the Ocean of Milk and purified by nectar, / and with the powder of the digits along with moonlight, the self-born [Brahmā] restored the moon as before.

2.s:
sa ṣoḍaśakalāpūrṇaḥ pūrvavadvibabhau yadā |
candrastadā sarvadevā mumudustasya darśanāt || 56 ||
2.d:
स षोडशकलापूर्णः पूर्ववद्विबभौ यदा ।
चन्द्रस्तदा सर्वदेवा मुमुदुस्तस्य दर्शनात् ॥ 56 ॥
2.m: When the moon shone as before, complete with sixteen digits, / then all the gods rejoiced at the sight of him.

2.s:
atha candrastadā pūrṇaḥ praṇipatya pitāmaham |
uvācedaṃ surasadomadhyago nāti harṣitaḥ || 57 ||
2.d:
अथ चन्द्रस्तदा पूर्णः प्रणिपत्य पितामहम् ।
उवाचेदं सुरसदोमध्यगो नाति हर्षितः ॥ 57 ॥
2.m: Then the moon, now full, bowed down to the grandfather / and, standing amidst the assembly of gods, spoke these words, not exceedingly joyful:

2.s: soma uvāca
2.d: सोम उवाच

2.s:
na sukhaṃ pūrvavad brahmañchaśarīre mama vartate |
na vīryaṃ vā tathotsāho niṣīdantyagasandhayaḥ || 58 ||
2.d:
न सुखं पूर्ववद् ब्रह्मञ्छशरीरे मम वर्तते ।
न वीर्यं वा तथोत्साहो निषीदन्त्यगसन्धयः ॥ 58 ॥
2.m: "There is no comfort in my body as before, O Brahmā, / nor strength, nor vigor; my joints sink down.

2.s:
notsahe pūrvavacceṣṭāṃ vidhātuṃ sutarāmaham |
ceṣṭāhīnastvanudina varteyaṃ kena lokakṛt || 59 ||
2.d:
नोत्सहे पूर्ववच्चेष्टां विधातुं सुतरामहम् ।
चेष्टाहीनस्त्वनुदिन वर्तेयं केन लोककृत् ॥ 59 ॥
2.m: I am entirely unable to make an effort as before. / Being devoid of effort day after day, how shall I exist, O creator of the world?"

2.s: brahmovāca
2.d: ब्रह्मोवाच

2.s:
grastasya yakṣmaṇā soma yadabhūdagasandhayaḥ |
pūrva viśīrṇā bhavatastatpūrṇamabhavannahi || 60 ||
2.d:
ग्रस्तस्य यक्ष्मणा सोम यदभूदगसन्धयः ।
पूर्व विशीर्णा भवतस्तत्पूर्णमभवन्नहि ॥ 60 ॥
2.m: "O Soma, when your joints were seized by consumption, / they were previously broken, and they did not become fully complete.

2.s:
adhunā bhavato dehacūrṇa niḥsārita mayā |
śarīrāt sāmṛtajyotsnāmañjasā rājayakṣmaṇaḥ || 61 ||
2.d:
अधुना भवतो देहचूर्ण निःसारित मया ।
शरीरात् सामृतज्योत्स्नामञ्जसा राजयक्ष्मणः ॥ 61 ॥
2.m: Now the powder of your body has been extracted by me / straight from the body of consumption, together with ambrosia and moonlight.

2.s:
teṣāṃ prakṣālanavidhau lavaśo yatsthitaṃ jale |
jyotsnāyāśca sudhāyāśca tena hīno bhavān yataḥ || 62 ||
2.d:
तेषां प्रक्षालनविधौ लवशो यत्स्थितं जले ।
ज्योत्स्नायाश्च सुधायाश्च तेन हीनो भवान् यतः ॥ 62 ॥
2.m: In the process of washing them, whatever particles remained in the water / of moonlight and nectar—because you are deprived of that,

2.s:
tato'ṅgasandhayo rājaṃstava sīdanti sāmpratam |
tasyopāyaṃ vidhāsyāmi yathā nāti labhedbhavān || 63 ||
2.d:
ततोऽङ्गसन्धयो राजंस्तव सीदन्ति साम्प्रतम् ।
तस्योपायं विधास्यामि यथा नाति लभेद्भवान् ॥ 63 ॥
2.m: therefore your joints are languishing now, O king. / I shall devise a remedy for it, so that you do not suffer greatly.

2.s:
prājāpatyaḥ puroḍāśo havanīyaḥ puro'dhvare |
endrastato'nu cāgneyaḥ pradeyaḥ sarvataḥ kratau || 64 ||
2.d:
प्राजापत्यः पुरोडाशो हवनीयः पुरोऽध्वरे ।
एन्द्रस्ततोऽनु चाग्नेयः प्रदेयः सर्वतः क्रतौ ॥ 64 ॥
2.m: A sacrificial cake dedicated to Prajāpati is to be offered first in the sacrifice; / thereafter one to Indra, and then one to Agni is to be offered all around in the rite.

2.s:
tato nu bhavato bhāgaḥ puroḍāśo mayā kṛtaḥ |
tena bhāgena buktena nityaṃ yajñakṛtena hi |
pūrvavat tai samutsāhaḥ śyāmavīryaṃ bhaviṣyati || 65 ||
2.d:
ततो नु भवतो भागः पुरोडाशो मया कृतः ।
तेन भागेन बुक्तेन नित्यं यज्ञकृतेन हि ।
पूर्ववत् तै समुत्साहः श्यामवीर्यं भविष्यति ॥ 65 ॥
2.m: After that, your share, a sacrificial cake, has been assigned by me. / By enjoying that share regularly made in the sacrifice, / your enthusiasm and vigor will indeed become as before.

2.s:
ye cāmṛtakaṇastoye kṣīrodasya sthitāstava |
śarīracūrṇaṃ vā yatte jyotsnāścāpi ye lavāḥ || 66 ||
2.d:
ये चामृतकणस्तोये क्षीरोदस्य स्थितास्तव ।
शरीरचूर्णं वा यत्ते ज्योत्स्नाश्चापि ये लवाः ॥ 66 ॥
2.m: And whatever particles of ambrosia of yours remain in the water of the Ocean of Milk, / or whatever body-powder of yours and particles of moonlight there are,

2.s:
tat sarvaṃ bhavato jyotsnāyogādanudinaṃ vidho |
vṛddhiṃ yāsyati satataṃ kṣīrasāgaragarbhagam || 67 ||
2.d:
तत् सर्वं भवतो ज्योत्स्नायोगादनुदिनं विधो ।
वृद्धिं यास्यति सततं क्षीरसागरगर्भगम् ॥ 67 ॥
2.m: all that, resting in the womb of the Ocean of Milk, O moon, / will constantly increase day after day through the conjunction of your moonlight.

2.s:
svārociṣe'ntare prāpte dvitīye śaṃkarāṃśajaḥ |
durvāsā bhavitā vipraḥ pracaṇḍaścaṇḍa bhānuvat || 68 ||
2.d:
स्वारोचिषेऽन्तरे प्राप्ते द्वितीये शंकरांशजः ।
दुर्वासा भविता विप्रः प्रचण्डश्चण्ड भानुवत् ॥ 68 ॥
2.m: When the second, Svārociṣa Manvantara arrives, / a brāhmaṇa named Durvāsas, born from a portion of Śaṅkara, will appear, fierce like the blazing sun.

2.s:
sa devendrasyāvinayācchāpaṃ datvā sudāruṇam |
kariṣyati tribhuvan niḥśrīkaṃ sasurāsuram || 69 ||
2.d:
स देवेन्द्रस्याविनयाच्छापं दत्वा सुदारुणम् ।
करिष्यति त्रिभुवन् निःश्रीकं ससुरासुरम् ॥ 69 ॥
2.m: Because of the insolence of the lord of gods, he, pronouncing a dreadful curse, / will render the three worlds, along with gods and asuras, devoid of fortune.

2.s:
śriyā hīne tato loke bhavitā lokaviplavaḥ |
yathā tava kṣayāt somaṃ pravṛtta sarvaviplavaḥ || 70 ||
2.d:
श्रिया हीने ततो लोके भविता लोकविप्लवः ।
यथा तव क्षयात् सोमं प्रवृत्त सर्वविप्लवः ॥ 70 ॥
2.m: When the world is bereft of fortune, there will be ruin of the world, / just as, O Soma, all-round ruin set in through your waning.

2.s:
tanmānuṣapramāṇena tṛtīye tu kṛte yugaṃ |
bhaviṣyati sthāsyati ca yāvad yugacatuṣṭayam || 71 ||
2.d:
तन्मानुषप्रमाणेन तृतीये तु कृते युगं ।
भविष्यति स्थास्यति च यावद् युगचतुष्टयम् ॥ 71 ॥
2.m: By human measure, it will occur in the third Kṛta Yuga, / and it will last as long as the four yugas.

2.s:
tataścaturthe samprāpte saha devai kṛte yuge |
kṣīrodaṃ nirmathiṣyāma śambhuviṣṇurahaṃ tathā || 72 ||
2.d:
ततश्चतुर्थे सम्प्राप्ते सह देवै कृते युगे ।
क्षीरोदं निर्मथिष्याम शम्भुविष्णुरहं तथा ॥ 72 ॥
2.m: Then, when the fourth Kṛta Yuga has arrived, / Śambhu, Viṣṇu, and I, together with the gods, shall churn the Ocean of Milk.

2.s:
manthānaṃ mandara kṛtvā netra kṛtvā tu vāsukīm |
yajñabhāgeṣu līneṣu devānnārthaṃ vayaṃ tataḥ |
mathiṣyāma samaṃ devai kṣīrodaṃ saha dānavaiḥ || 73 ||
2.d:
मन्थानं मन्दर कृत्वा नेत्र कृत्वा तु वासुकीम् ।
यज्ञभागेषु लीनेषु देवान्नार्थं वयं ततः ।
मथिष्याम समं देवै क्षीरोदं सह दानवैः ॥ 73 ॥
2.m: Making Mandara the churning rod and Vāsuki the churning rope, / when the sacrificial shares have vanished, for the sake of the gods' food / we shall then churn the Ocean of Milk together with the gods and dānavas.

2.s:
tvaccharīrāmṛtamidaṃ yatsthitaṃ kṣīrasāgare |
tat pramathya grahīṣyāmo rāśībhūtaṃ tathā kṣayam || 74 ||
2.d:
त्वच्छरीरामृतमिदं यत्स्थितं क्षीरसागरे ।
तत् प्रमथ्य ग्रहीष्यामो राशीभूतं तथा क्षयम् ॥ 74 ॥
2.m: This ambrosia of your body which lies in the Ocean of Milk— / having churned it thoroughly, we will take that collected mass, as well as the loss.

2.s:
sarvauṣadhyantare kṛtvā tvaccharīraṃ tadā vayam |
kṣepsyāmaḥ sāgarajale śarīrārthaṃ vidho tava || 75 ||
2.d:
सर्वौषध्यन्तरे कृत्वा त्वच्छरीरं तदा वयम् ।
क्षेप्स्यामः सागरजले शरीरार्थं विधो तव ॥ 75 ॥
2.m: Placing inside all the herbs, we will then cast your body / into the ocean's water for the sake of your body, O moon.

2.s:
nirmathya sāgaraṃ paścāt samuddhārya yadāmṛtam |
tadā tava vapustasmin pūrvavat sambhaviṣyati || 76 ||
2.d:
निर्मथ्य सागरं पश्चात् समुद्धार्य यदामृतम् ।
तदा तव वपुस्तस्मिन् पूर्ववत् सम्भविष्यति ॥ 76 ॥
2.m: After churning the ocean, when the ambrosia is drawn forth, / then your body will become just as it was before.

2.s:
ojovīryādbhutaṃ kāntamakṣayaṃ ca sudhātmakam |
dṛḍhāṃgasandhikaṃ cāru bhaviṣyati vapustava || 77 ||
2.d:
ओजोवीर्याद्भुतं कान्तमक्षयं च सुधात्मकम् ।
दृढांगसन्धिकं चारु भविष्यति वपुस्तव ॥ 77 ॥
2.m: Your body will become endowed with wonderful vitality and strength, / radiant, imperishable, consisting of nectar, firm in its joints, and beautiful."

2.s: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
2.d: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

2.s:
sudhāṃśumevamābhāṣya brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ |
vidhoḥ kṣayāya māsārdhaṃ vṛddhaye yatnavānabhūt || 78 ||
2.d:
सुधांशुमेवमाभाष्य ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ।
विधोः क्षयाय मासार्धं वृद्धये यत्नवानभूत् ॥ 78 ॥
2.m: Having thus addressed the nectar-rayed [moon], Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / made an effort for the waning of the moon for half a month and for its waxing.

2.s:
yathā dakṣeṇa gaditaṃ māsārdhaṃ yātu candramāḥ |
kṣayaṃ vṛddhiṃ ca māsārdhaṃ yatnaṃ tatrākarodvidhiḥ || 79 ||
2.d:
यथा दक्षेण गदितं मासार्धं यातु चन्द्रमाः ।
क्षयं वृद्धिं च मासार्धं यत्नं तत्राकरोद्विधिः ॥ 79 ॥
2.m: Just as Dakṣa had spoken, that the moon should go to wane / for half a month and to wax for half a month, Vidhi made the arrangement there.

2.s:
tatah ṣoḍaśadhā candraṃ surajyeṣṭho vibhaktavān |
vibhajya ca surān sarvān samuvācedamuttamam || 80 ||
brahmovāca
2.d:
ततह् षोडशधा चन्द्रं सुरज्येष्ठो विभक्तवान् ।
विभज्य च सुरान् सर्वान् समुवाचेदमुत्तमम् ॥ 80 ॥
ब्रह्मोवाच
2.m: Then the eldest of the gods divided the moon into sixteen parts; / and having divided it, he spoke these excellent [words] to all the gods: / Brahmā said:

2.s:
kalāḥ ṣoḍaśa candrasya tatrekā śambhumūrdhani |
tiṣṭhatvadyāvadhi parā kṣaya yāntu kṣaya vinā || 81 ||
2.d:
कलाः षोडश चन्द्रस्य तत्रेका शम्भुमूर्धनि ।
तिष्ठत्वद्यावधि परा क्षय यान्तु क्षय विना ॥ 81 ॥
2.m: "The digits of the moon are sixteen; let one among them remain on Śambhu’s head / from this day onward; let the others undergo waning without being destroyed.

2.s:
kṣayeṇa yadi rogeṇa māsārdhaṃ dakṣavākyata |
kṣayāya pīḍyate candro nopaśāntistadā bhavet || 82 ||
2.d:
क्षयेण यदि रोगेण मासार्धं दक्षवाक्यत ।
क्षयाय पीड्यते चन्द्रो नोपशान्तिस्तदा भवेत् ॥ 82 ॥
2.m: If by the disease of consumption, in accordance with Dakṣa’s words, / the moon were afflicted for half a month to its destruction, then there would be no alleviation.

2.s:
kiṃtvasya yā kalā śambhau jyotsnā gacchatu tā prati |
caturdaśakalāsaṃsthāḥ pratimāsaṃ surottamāḥ || 83 ||
2.d:
किंत्वस्य या कला शम्भौ ज्योत्स्ना गच्छतु ता प्रति ।
चतुर्दशकलासंस्थाः प्रतिमासं सुरोत्तमाः ॥ 83 ॥
2.m:
However, that digit of his which is on Śambhu—let the moonlight go to it; / O best of gods, residing in the fourteen digits each month,

do drink those [portions] consisting of the fourteen digits, / beginning from the first lunar day up to the fourteenth day.

2.s:
caturdaśakalāsaṃsthānyabhūtāni pivantu vai |
pratipattithimārabhya bhavantastāṃ caturdaśīm || 84 ||
2.d:
चतुर्दशकलासंस्थान्यभूतानि पिवन्तु वै ।
प्रतिपत्तिथिमारभ्य भवन्तस्तां चतुर्दशीम् ॥ 84 ॥

2.s:
tejobhāgāḥ sūryabimbaṃ caturdaśatithau kramāt |
praviśantu kṣayaṃ tvevaṃ kṛṣṇapakṣe vidhorbhavet || 85 ||
2.d:
तेजोभागाः सूर्यबिम्बं चतुर्दशतिथौ क्रमात् ।
प्रविशन्तु क्षयं त्वेवं कृष्णपक्षे विधोर्भवेत् ॥ 85 ॥
2.m: Let the shares of radiant energy successively enter the solar orb on the fourteenth lunar day; / thus indeed let there be the waning of the moon in the dark fortnight.

2.s:
yātu śeṣā kalā darśe haritpatre palāyitā |
tiṣṭhatu prathame bhāge tithau tasyāṃ niśāpateḥ || 86 ||
2.d:
यातु शेषा कला दर्शे हरित्पत्रे पलायिता ।
तिष्ठतु प्रथमे भागे तिथौ तस्यां निशापतेः ॥ 86 ॥
2.m: Let the remaining digit on the new-moon day, taking refuge in green leaves, / abide in the first part on that lunar day of the lord of the night.

2.s:
dvitīye darśabhāge tu rohiṇyā yātu mandiram |
tṛtīye tu sarasvatyāṃ snātvā samutthito vidhuḥ || 87 ||
2.d:
द्वितीये दर्शभागे तु रोहिण्या यातु मन्दिरम् ।
तृतीये तु सरस्वत्यां स्नात्वा समुत्थितो विधुः ॥ 87 ॥
2.m: In the second part of the new moon, let it go to Rohiṇī’s mansion; / in the third [part], having bathed in the Sarasvatī, the moon rises up.

2.s:
caturthe balasampūrṇastithibhāge vibhāvasoḥ |
maṇḍalaṃ yātu candro'yaṃ sabimbarathaghoṭakaḥ || 88 ||
2.d:
चतुर्थे बलसम्पूर्णस्तिथिभागे विभावसोः ।
मण्डलं यातु चन्द्रोऽयं सबिम्बरथघोटकः ॥ 88 ॥
2.m: Filled with strength in the fourth part of the lunar day, let this moon, / together with its orb, chariot, and horses, enter the solar orb.

2.s:
yāvat kālena hi kalā prathamā kṣayamāpnuyāt |
evamevaṃ kṛṣṇapakṣe tāvat sā pratipad bhavet || 89 ||
2.d:
यावत् कालेन हि कला प्रथमा क्षयमाप्नुयात् ।
एवमेवं कृष्णपक्षे तावत् सा प्रतिपद् भवेत् ॥ 89 ॥
2.m: In as much time as the first digit undergoes waning, / so long, in this manner, shall be that first lunar day in the dark fortnight.

2.s:
dvitīyādau kṛṣṇapakṣe vṛddhi-hrāsastathāvidhaḥ |
tithīnāṃ vṛddhihetuśca śukle kṛṣṇe tathā bhavet || 90 ||
2.d:
द्वितीयादौ कृष्णपक्षे वृद्धि-ह्रासस्तथाविधः ।
तिथीनां वृद्धिहेतुश्च शुक्ले कृष्णे तथा भवेत् ॥ 90 ॥
2.m: From the second [tithi] onward in the dark fortnight, increase and decrease are of that sort; / and the cause of the increase of the lunar days shall be likewise in the bright and the dark [fortnights].

2.s:
tataḥ punaḥ śuklapakṣe yāvat pūrvakaloditā |
vṛddhiṃ naiti bhavettāvat pratipattitithirāditaḥ || 91 ||
2.d:
ततः पुनः शुक्लपक्षे यावत् पूर्वकलोदिता ।
वृद्धिं नैति भवेत्तावत् प्रतिपत्तितिथिरादितः ॥ 91 ॥
2.m: Then again in the bright fortnight, as long as the previous digit that has risen / does not attain increase, so long shall be the first lunar day from the beginning.

2.s:
tato dvitīyabhāgasya yā jyotsnā haramūrdhani |
sthitā yā vai kalā yātu gatā sāpunareṣyati |
yuṣmābhistu bhavet peyamamṛtaṃ yaddine dine || 92 ||
2.d:
ततो द्वितीयभागस्य या ज्योत्स्ना हरमूर्धनि ।
स्थिता या वै कला यातु गता सापुनरेष्यति ।
युष्माभिस्तु भवेत् पेयममृतं यद्दिने दिने ॥ 92 ॥
2.m: Then, of the second part, whatever moonlight is on Hara’s head, / whichever digit is situated there, let it depart; having departed, it will return again; / and the nectar which you must drink day after day,

2.s:
taddvitīyāditithibhiḥ pūrṇāntābhiḥ sadaiva hi |
svayamutpatsyate candro jyotsnāyogāt surottamāḥ || 93 ||
2.d:
तद्द्वितीयादितिथिभिः पूर्णान्ताभिः सदैव हि ।
स्वयमुत्पत्स्यते चन्द्रो ज्योत्स्नायोगात् सुरोत्तमाः ॥ 93 ॥
2.m: by those lunar days beginning with the second and ending with the full moon, always indeed / the moon will arise by itself from the union with moonlight, O best of gods.

2.s:
yathā dine dine bhāgāḥ kṣaya yānti tathā vidhoḥ |
vṛddhi gacchantyanudinaṃ śuklapakṣe'nvahaṃ surāḥ || 94 ||
2.d:
यथा दिने दिने भागाः क्षय यान्ति तथा विधोः ।
वृद्धि गच्छन्त्यनुदिनं शुक्लपक्षेऽन्वहं सुराः ॥ 94 ॥
2.m: Just as day after day the portions of the moon undergo waning, / so day after day they undergo increase in the bright fortnight, O gods.

2.s:
tejobhāga sūryabimbāt punareva sameṣyati |
prayāsyati kṛṣṇapakṣe yathā bhāgakramaṃ tathā || 95 ||
2.d:
तेजोभाग सूर्यबिम्बात् पुनरेव समेष्यति ।
प्रयास्यति कृष्णपक्षे यथा भागक्रमं तथा ॥ 95 ॥
2.m: The share of radiant energy will return again from the solar orb, / just as it departs in the dark fortnight according to the sequence of parts.

2.s:
jyotsnā haraśiraścandrāt pratyahaṃ punareṣyati |
tejobhāgaḥ sūryabimbādamṛtaṃ varṣati svayam || 96 ||
2.d:
ज्योत्स्ना हरशिरश्चन्द्रात् प्रत्यहं पुनरेष्यति ।
तेजोभागः सूर्यबिम्बादमृतं वर्षति स्वयम् ॥ 96 ॥
2.m: The moonlight will return each day from the moon on Hara’s head; / the share of radiant energy from the solar orb rains down nectar of its own accord.

2.s:
evaṃ vṛddhiḥ śuklapakṣe sudhāṃśauḥ sambhaviṣyati |
pakṣayoḥ śuklakṛṣṇatvaṃ candravṛddhikṣayādbhavet || 97 ||
2.d:
एवं वृद्धिः शुक्लपक्षे सुधांशौः सम्भविष्यति ।
पक्षयोः शुक्लकृष्णत्वं चन्द्रवृद्धिक्षयाद्भवेत् ॥ 97 ॥
2.m: Thus the increase of the nectar-rayed [moon] will occur in the bright fortnight; / the quality of being bright and dark of the two fortnights arises from the waxing and waning of the moon.

2.s:
yāvat kālena yo bhāgaḥ kṣayaṃ vṛddhiṃ ca yāsyati |
tāvat kālamabhivyāpya tithiḥ sthāsyati sā punaḥ || 98 ||
2.d:
यावत् कालेन यो भागः क्षयं वृद्धिं च यास्यति ।
तावत् कालमभिव्याप्य तिथिः स्थास्यति सा पुनः ॥ 98 ॥
2.m: In as much time as any portion goes to waning and waxing, / spanning that amount of time that lunar day will stand again.

2.s:
cireṇa viddhiryadi vā kṣayo vā drutena vṛddhiryadivā kṣayo vā |
drutāttithīnāntu sadā kṣayaḥ syāccirātu vṛddhistithiṣu praveśe || 99 ||
2.d:
